regime: NAIC Annual Statement Blank / Statutory Accounting (AP&P Manual)
title: File statutory annual statement (Blank) with domiciliary regulator and NAIC by March 1
requirement: Every domestic insurer must prepare and file its statutory annual financial statement on the prescribed NAIC Annual Statement Blank, together with all required supplements, with its state of domicile and the NAIC on or before March 1 for the preceding calendar year. Statements must be prepared in conformity with the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (SSAPs). Filing the complete, timely, accurate blank is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (SSAPs)
sourceNote: Verified content.naic.org Statutory Accounting Principles topic + 2025/2026 Annual Statement Instructions; March 1 deadline current for 2026 filings.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state via financial reporting statutes; NAIC accreditation standard.

title: File statutory quarterly statements on the NAIC Quarterly Blank each quarter
requirement: Every domestic insurer must prepare and file quarterly statutory financial statements on the NAIC Quarterly Statement Blank for the first three calendar quarters, generally due 45 days after quarter-end (May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15), prepared under the AP&P Manual/SSAPs. Timely, complete quarterly filing with the domiciliary state and NAIC is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Quarterly Statement Instructions (P/C, Life, Health, Title)
sourceNote: Verified 2026 NAIC Quarterly Statement Instructions on content.naic.org; quarterly blank framework current.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; NAIC accreditation standard.

regime: Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205 / Model Audit Rule)
title: File CPA-audited statutory financial statements by June 1 (Model 205)
requirement: Every insurer meeting the premium thresholds must have its statutory financial statements audited annually by an independent certified public accountant and file the audited financial report with the commissioner by June 1 following the December 31 year-end. The audit must be conducted per the Model Audit Rule requirements. Timely filing of the audited report is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 205 (Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation), Sec. 4
sourceNote: Verified Model 205 PDF on content.naic.org; June 1 audited-report deadline current; NAIC accreditation standard.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205 / Model Audit Rule)
title: File Management's Report of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (Model 205)
requirement: Every insurer (or group) with annual direct-written and assumed premiums of $500 million or more must prepare Management's Report of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting as of the prior December 31 and file it with the commissioner within 60 days after the audited financial report is filed (by August 1). The report must attest to the effectiveness of internal controls over financial reporting.
citation: NAIC Model 205, Sec. 16 (Management's Report of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting)
sourceNote: Verified Model 205 on content.naic.org; $500M threshold and Aug 1 (60-day) filing window current.
regime_note: SOX-analog for insurers; adopted state-by-state.

regime: Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205 / Model Audit Rule)
title: Maintain Audit Committee with required independent-member supermajority (Model 205)
requirement: Insurers must establish an Audit Committee of the board to oversee the CPA audit. For insurers with over $500 million in prior-year direct-written and assumed premiums, at least 75% of Audit Committee members must be independent; for $300M-$500M, at least 50% must be independent. The committee must be directly responsible for appointment, compensation and oversight of the independent CPA.
citation: NAIC Model 205, Sec. 14 (Requirements for Audit Committees)
sourceNote: Verified Model 205 Sec. 14 independence tiers (75%/50%) on content.naic.org; in effect since Jan 1, 2010.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205 / Model Audit Rule)
title: Rotate lead audit partner every five years with five-year cooling-off (Model 205)
requirement: The lead (coordinating) audit partner with primary responsibility for the insurer's statutory audit may not act in that capacity for more than five consecutive years, after which that partner must observe a five-year cooling-off period before serving the company or its insurance subsidiaries/affiliates again. Compliance with the rotation and independence rules is a condition of an acceptable audit.
citation: NAIC Model 205, Sec. 7D (Qualifications of Independent CPA / lead partner rotation)
sourceNote: Verified Model 205 Sec. 7 five-year lead-partner rotation and cooling-off on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure Model Act (Model 305) & Regulation (Model 306)
title: File confidential Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure (CGAD) by June 1 (Model 305)
requirement: An insurer or insurer group must file a confidential Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure with the lead state and/or domestic regulator by June 1 each year, providing narrative and sample documentation on its corporate governance framework, board policies, and internal oversight practices. Failure to timely file may subject the insurer to a penalty.
citation: NAIC Model 305 (Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure Model Act)
sourceNote: Verified Model 305 on content.naic.org; June 1 deadline; NAIC accreditation requirement since Jan 1, 2020.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model 440)
title: File annual holding-company registration statement (Form B) (Model 440)
requirement: Every insurer that is a member of an insurance holding company system must register with the commissioner and file an annual registration statement (Form B) containing current information about the holding company system's capital structure, ownership, affiliates, and material transactions. Timely annual filing of accurate Form B information is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 4 (Registration of Insurers); Model 450 Form B
sourceNote: Verified Model 440 registration requirement and Form B on content.naic.org; NAIC accreditation standard.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; forms in Model 450 regulation.

regime: Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model 440)
title: File Form C summary of registration-statement changes (Model 440)
requirement: An insurer required to file an annual Form B registration statement must also furnish Form C, a summary outlining all items in the current registration statement that represent changes from the prior year's filing. Form C accompanies the annual Form B and must be filed with the domiciliary commissioner.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 4; Model 450 Form C
sourceNote: Verified Model 440 Sec. 4 / Form C requirement on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; Form C in Model 450 regulation.

regime: Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model 440)
title: File prior notice of material affiliated transactions (Form D) (Model 440)
requirement: A registered insurer must file a Form D notice with the commissioner and receive non-disapproval before entering into specified material transactions with affiliates (e.g., sales/exchanges/loans exceeding thresholds, reinsurance agreements, management/service contracts, cost-sharing arrangements). The transaction may not proceed until the standstill/approval period lapses without disapproval.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 5 (Standards and Management of an Insurer within a Holding Company System); Model 450 Form D
sourceNote: Verified Model 440 affiliated-transaction prior-notice (Form D) requirement on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; Form D in Model 450 regulation.

regime: Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model 440)
title: File annual Enterprise Risk Report (Form F) by ultimate controlling person (Model 440)
requirement: The ultimate controlling person of every insurer subject to registration must file an annual Enterprise Risk Report (Form F) with the lead state commissioner, identifying material risks within the insurance holding company system that could pose enterprise risk to the insurers. Timely annual Form F filing to the lead state is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 4L (Enterprise Risk Report / Form F)
sourceNote: Verified Model 440 Form F enterprise risk report; NAIC accreditation-effective Jan 1, 2016 per content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regulatorName: Acquiring party filing with domiciliary commissioner
regime: Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model 440)
title: File Form A and obtain approval before acquiring control of a domestic insurer (Model 440)
requirement: Any person seeking to acquire control of, or merge with, a domestic insurer must file a Form A statement with the commissioner and obtain prior approval after a public hearing. The acquisition of control may not be consummated until the commissioner approves; the filing must disclose the acquirer's identity, background, financing, and plans for the insurer.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 3 (Acquisition of Control of or Merger with Domestic Insurer); Model 450 Form A
sourceNote: Verified Model 440 Sec. 3 Form A change-of-control approval on content.naic.org; UCAA Form A.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; Form A in Model 450 regulation / UCAA.

regime: Group Capital Calculation (2020 revisions to Model 440/450)
title: File annual Group Capital Calculation (GCC) with lead state (Model 440)
requirement: The ultimate controlling person of an insurance group subject to registration must file an annual Group Capital Calculation with the lead state commissioner, aggregating available and required capital across the group using the NAIC GCC template and instructions. The GCC provides regulators a group-wide capital adequacy view. Timely annual filing is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 440, Sec. 4 (Group Capital Calculation, 2020 revisions)
sourceNote: Verified 2020 Model 440/450 GCC revisions on content.naic.org; became NAIC accreditation requirement effective Jan 1, 2026.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; accreditation-effective 2026.

regime: Liquidity Stress Test Framework (2020 revisions to Model 440/450)
title: File annual Liquidity Stress Test results for in-scope large life insurers (Model 440)
requirement: The ultimate controlling person of an insurance group whose life insurers meet the NAIC Liquidity Stress Test in-scope criteria must file annual LST results with the lead state commissioner under the NAIC LST Framework, providing macroprudential insight into group liquidity risk. Timely filing of the LST for the scoped data year is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 440 (2020 revisions, Liquidity Stress Test); NAIC LST Framework
sourceNote: Verified 2020 Model 440/450 LST revisions on content.naic.org; scoped to certain large life groups; accreditation-linked.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; applies to in-scope large life insurers only.

regime: Risk-Based Capital (RBC) For Insurers Model Act (Model 312)
title: File annual Risk-Based Capital report by March 1 (Model 312)
requirement: Every domestic insurer must, on or prior to each March 1, prepare and submit to the commissioner an RBC report of its total adjusted capital and RBC levels as of the prior calendar year-end, computed using the applicable NAIC RBC instructions (life, P/C, or health formula). The report triggers regulatory action levels (Company/Regulatory/Authorized Control/Mandatory Control) based on the RBC ratio.
citation: NAIC Model 312 (Risk-Based Capital For Insurers Model Act), Sec. 2
sourceNote: Verified Model 312 Sec. 2 March 1 RBC report deadline on content.naic.org; adopted 1993, latest revision 2012; NAIC accreditation standard.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Risk Management and Own Risk and Solvency Assessment Model Act (Model 505)
title: File annual ORSA Summary Report with lead state (Model 505)
requirement: An insurer or insurance group meeting the premium-size threshold must conduct an Own Risk and Solvency Assessment at least annually and file a confidential ORSA Summary Report with the lead state commissioner upon request (at least annually for scoped groups), assessing material risks, the ERM framework, and prospective solvency/capital adequacy consistent with the NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual.
citation: NAIC Model 505 (Risk Management and Own Risk and Solvency Assessment Model Act), Sec. 4-5
sourceNote: Verified Model 505 and NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual on content.naic.org; confidential summary report; NAIC accreditation standard.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; threshold-scoped (generally >$500M individual / >$1B group premium).

regime: Standard Valuation Law (Model 820) / Valuation Manual VM-30
title: File annual Statement of Actuarial Opinion on life reserves via appointed actuary (Model 820)
requirement: Every life insurer must annually have its appointed actuary issue a Statement of Actuarial Opinion, filed with the annual statement, opining that the aggregate reserves and related actuarial items make good and sufficient provision for the company's obligations, based on an asset adequacy analysis where required, in accordance with the Standard Valuation Law and Valuation Manual (VM-30).
citation: NAIC Model 820 (Standard Valuation Law), Sec. 3; Valuation Manual VM-30
sourceNote: Verified 2026 Valuation Manual (VM-30 actuarial opinion) on content.naic.org; SVL operative with the Valuation Manual.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; SVL is NAIC accreditation standard.

regime: Valuation Manual VM-20 (Principle-Based Reserving for Life Products)
title: Calculate principle-based reserves for covered life products under VM-20
requirement: For in-scope life insurance policies issued on or after the PBR operative date, the insurer must compute minimum reserves using the principle-based methodology of VM-20 (net premium reserve plus deterministic and stochastic reserve components, subject to exclusion tests), reflecting company-specific and prescribed assumptions. Compliant PBR reserves must be reported in the annual statement.
citation: NAIC Valuation Manual, VM-20 (Requirements for Principle-Based Reserves for Life Products)
sourceNote: Verified VM-20 in Jan 1, 2026 Valuation Manual edition on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted via Standard Valuation Law; mandatory since 2020 PBR full phase-in.

regime: Valuation Manual VM-21 (Principle-Based Reserving for Variable Annuities)
title: Calculate principle-based reserves for variable annuities under VM-21
requirement: Insurers writing variable annuities and similar guaranteed-benefit products must compute statutory reserves using the stochastic, principle-based methodology of VM-21 (conditional tail expectation amount plus additional standard projection amount). Compliant VM-21 reserves must be established and reported in the annual statement.
citation: NAIC Valuation Manual, VM-21 (Requirements for Principle-Based Reserves for Variable Annuities)
sourceNote: Verified VM-21 in Jan 1, 2026 Valuation Manual edition on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted via Standard Valuation Law.

title: Prepare and file the PBR Actuarial Report documenting reserves under VM-31
requirement: For policies subject to principle-based reserving, the qualified actuary must prepare a PBR Actuarial Report per VM-31 documenting the reserve methodology, assumptions, models, governance, and results in sufficient detail for regulatory review, and make it available to the domiciliary commissioner. Complete VM-31 documentation supporting the reported PBR reserves is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Valuation Manual, VM-31 (PBR Actuarial Report Requirements)
sourceNote: Verified VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report in Jan 1, 2026 Valuation Manual on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted via Standard Valuation Law.

regime: Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation (Model 822) / P&C Annual Statement Instructions
title: File annual P&C Statement of Actuarial Opinion on loss and LAE reserves (Model 822)
requirement: Every property/casualty insurer must have its appointed actuary issue an annual Statement of Actuarial Opinion on the reasonableness of the company's loss and loss adjustment expense reserves, filed with the annual statement, together with an Actuarial Opinion Summary and supporting Actuarial Report/memorandum conforming to Actuarial Standards Board standards of practice.
citation: NAIC Model 822 (Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation); P/C Annual Statement Instructions
sourceNote: Verified Model 822 AOMR and 2025 P/C Annual Statement Instructions (SAO) on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; P&C SAO also embedded in Annual Statement Instructions.

title: Retain actuarial opinion supporting documentation for seven years (Model 822)
requirement: The appointed actuary must retain on file, for at least seven years, documentation sufficient to determine the procedures followed, analyses performed, bases for assumptions, and results obtained in support of the Statement of Actuarial Opinion and memorandum, and make it available to the commissioner on request.
sourceNote: Verified Model 822 seven-year documentation-retention requirement on content.naic.org.
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state.

regime: Investments of Insurers Model Act (Defined Limits Version, Model 280)
title: Maintain diversification limits on general investments (Model 280)
requirement: Insurers must limit aggregate investments in medium/lower-grade and other categories and observe general diversification thresholds (e.g., a 3% single-issuer/general diversification limit for life insurers and 5% for P/C insurers) as prescribed by the Investments of Insurers Model Act, keeping the portfolio within admitted-asset percentage caps. Ongoing compliance with the statutory limits is the pass condition.
citation: NAIC Model 280 (Investments of Insurers Model Act — Defined Limits Version), diversification sections
sourceNote: Verified Model 280 general 3%/5% diversification limits on content.naic.org; adopted state-by-state (some states use Model 283 Defined Standards version).
regime_note: Adopted state-by-state; Model 280 (defined limits) vs Model 283 (defined standards) alternatives.

regime: NAIC Securities Valuation Office (SVO) / Purposes and Procedures Manual
title: File eligible securities with the NAIC SVO and report assigned NAIC Designations
requirement: Insurers must file eligible reported securities that are not otherwise exempt or automatically designated with the NAIC Securities Valuation Office for credit assessment, and report the resulting NAIC Designations on the annual statement investment schedules, as prescribed by the Purposes and Procedures Manual of the NAIC Investment Analysis Office. The designations drive RBC charges, admissibility, and reported carrying values.
citation: Purposes and Procedures Manual of the NAIC Investment Analysis Office (SVO)
sourceNote: Verified SVO role and 2026 Purposes and Procedures Manual on content.naic.org; SVO designates ~200,000 securities annually.
regime_note: Applies via annual statement/SSAP framework; adopted state-by-state through statutory accounting.

title: CEO/CFO principal-officer certification of each periodic report (SOX §302)
requirement: The principal executive and principal financial officers of the SEC-registered parent must each personally certify in every Form 10-K and 10-Q that the report does not contain material misstatements/omissions, that the financials fairly present the issuer's condition, and that they are responsible for and have evaluated disclosure controls. Certifications are filed as exhibits 31.1/31.2. Pass = signed certifications accompany each periodic report.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR 240.13a-14 and SEC 2003 adopting release; in force as of 2026.

title: Management's annual assessment of internal control over financial reporting (SOX §404(a))
requirement: Management must include in the annual Form 10-K a report stating its responsibility for ICFR and its assessment, as of fiscal year-end, of the effectiveness of the issuer's internal control over financial reporting using a recognized framework. Pass = management's ICFR report is included and the assessment is supported.
sourceNote: Verified SEC 2003 final rule (33-8238) and eCFR 17 CFR 240.13a-15; in force 2026.

title: Auditor attestation on ICFR for accelerated/large-accelerated filer (SOX §404(b))
requirement: As a large-accelerated filer, the issuer's registered public accounting firm must attest to and report on the effectiveness of the issuer's internal control over financial reporting; the auditor's attestation is filed with the annual Form 10-K. Pass = auditor's ICFR attestation report accompanies the 10-K.
sourceNote: Verified 15 U.S.C. 7262(b); large-accelerated filers are not exempt (only non-accelerated/EGCs are). In force 2026.

title: File annual report on Form 10-K each fiscal year
requirement: Every issuer with securities registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act must file an annual report on Form 10-K after each full fiscal year, containing audited financial statements and required Reg S-K/S-X disclosures. Large-accelerated filers must file within 60 days of fiscal year-end. Pass = timely, complete 10-K filed on EDGAR.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR 240.13a-1; in force 2026.

title: File quarterly report on Form 10-Q for each of the first three fiscal quarters
requirement: The issuer must file a Form 10-Q for each of the first three fiscal quarters, containing unaudited interim financial statements and MD&A. Large-accelerated filers must file within 40 days of quarter-end. Pass = timely, complete 10-Q filed on EDGAR each quarter.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR 240.13a-13; in force 2026.

title: File current report on Form 8-K within four business days of triggering events
requirement: The issuer must file a Form 8-K to disclose specified material corporate events (e.g., material agreements, results of operations, departures of directors/officers, changes in auditor) generally within four business days of the triggering event. Pass = 8-K filed for each enumerated event within the applicable deadline.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR Part 240 Subpart A (Form 8-K general instructions); in force 2026.

title: File and furnish definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) for shareholder meetings
requirement: When soliciting proxies for a shareholder meeting (including the annual meeting), the issuer must file a proxy statement conforming to Schedule 14A with the SEC and furnish it to security holders, preceded by a preliminary filing where required. Pass = compliant DEF 14A filed and delivered before solicitation/voting.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR 240.14a-101 Schedule 14A; in force 2026.

title: Disclose pay-versus-performance table in the proxy statement (Item 402(v))
requirement: In proxy and information statements requiring executive compensation disclosure, the issuer must include a table relating compensation actually paid to named executives against total shareholder return, net income, and a company-selected measure over the most recent fiscal years, plus a list of its most important performance measures. Pass = complete Item 402(v) disclosure in the DEF 14A.
sourceNote: Verified SEC final rule 34-95607 (eff. Oct 11, 2022; first proxies for FYs ending on/after Dec 16, 2022). In force 2026.

title: Adopt, file, and disclose an incentive-compensation clawback policy (Rule 10D-1)
requirement: As a listed issuer, the group must maintain a written clawback policy requiring recovery of erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation from current/former executive officers following an accounting restatement, file the policy as an exhibit to its Form 10-K, and annually disclose any recovery activity. Pass = compliant policy filed and clawback disclosures made.
sourceNote: Verified SEC Rule 10D-1; exchange listing standards effective Oct 2, 2023, policy adoption by Dec 1, 2023. In force 2026.

title: Report material cybersecurity incidents on Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days
requirement: Upon determining that a cybersecurity incident is material, the issuer must file a Form 8-K under Item 1.05 within four business days describing the incident's nature, scope, timing, and material impact (subject to a national-security delay by the U.S. Attorney General). Pass = timely, compliant Item 1.05 8-K filed after each materiality determination.
sourceNote: Verified SEC final rule (33-11216); Item 1.05 compliance began Dec 18, 2023 (SRCs June 15, 2024). In force 2026.

regime: Regulation S-K Item 106 (Cybersecurity Risk Management & Governance)
title: Disclose cybersecurity risk management, strategy, and board governance in Form 10-K
requirement: The issuer must describe in its annual Form 10-K its processes for assessing, identifying, and managing material cybersecurity risks, material effects of risks/incidents, and the board's and management's oversight roles in cybersecurity. Pass = complete Item 106 narrative included in the 10-K.
sourceNote: Verified SEC final rule (33-11216); Item 106 annual-report disclosure required for FYs ending on/after Dec 15, 2023. In force 2026.

title: SEC-registered adviser fiduciary duty and Form ADV registration/amendment
requirement: Any group affiliate acting as an SEC-registered investment adviser must register on Form ADV, owes clients a fiduciary duty (duties of care and loyalty) under the antifraud provisions, and must not engage in fraudulent, deceptive, or manipulative conduct. Pass = current Form ADV on file and conduct consistent with the fiduciary standard.
sourceNote: Verified Advisers Act §206 and SEC fiduciary interpretation IA-5248 (2019). In force 2026.

title: File Form ADV annual updating amendment within 90 days of fiscal year-end
requirement: An SEC-registered adviser affiliate must amend Form ADV at least annually, within 90 days after the end of its fiscal year, and more frequently to correct materially inaccurate information (other-than-annual amendments). Pass = timely annual updating amendment filed via IARD.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 17 CFR 275.204-1; in force 2026.

regime: Investment Company Act of 1940 (Variable Annuity Separate Account)
title: Register variable annuity separate account and offer contracts on Form N-4
requirement: An insurance-company separate account funding variable annuity contracts must register as an investment company under the 1940 Act (typically a unit investment trust) and register the contracts/interests under the Securities Act on Form N-4, providing the prescribed layered prospectus disclosure. Pass = effective N-4 registration and current prospectus for offered variable annuities.
sourceNote: Verified SEC Form N-4 rulemaking (33-11294, 2024) covering variable/index-linked/RMVA annuities. In force 2026.

regime: Investment Company Act of 1940 (Variable Life Separate Account)
title: Register variable life insurance separate account and offer policies on Form N-6
requirement: An insurance-company separate account registered as a unit investment trust that funds variable life insurance policies must register the policies/interests on Form N-6 and provide the tailored variable-life prospectus disclosure. Pass = effective N-6 registration and current prospectus for offered variable life policies.
sourceNote: Verified SEC Rule 498A / Form N-6 disclosure rulemaking (2020). In force 2026.

regime: PCAOB AS 3101 (Auditor's Report / Critical Audit Matters)
title: Auditor communicates critical audit matters in the issuer's audit report (AS 3101)
requirement: The issuer's registered public accounting firm must issue an auditor's report conforming to AS 3101, including a separate section communicating critical audit matters arising from the current-period audit (matters involving especially challenging, subjective, or complex auditor judgment) or stating that there are none. Pass = CAM-compliant auditor's report filed with the 10-K.
sourceNote: Verified PCAOB AS 3101; CAM requirements effective large-accelerated filers FYs ending on/after Jun 30, 2019, others Dec 15, 2020. In force 2026.

title: Auditor retains audit and review records for seven years (SOX §802 / Rule 2-06)
requirement: The accounting firm auditing or reviewing the issuer's financial statements must retain workpapers and records forming the basis of, or documenting conclusions/opinions related to, the audit or review for seven years after the auditor concludes the engagement. Pass = retention program meets the seven-year Rule 2-06 standard.
sourceNote: Verified SEC final rule 33-8180 implementing SOX §802 (Reg S-X 2-06, seven-year retention). In force 2026.

regime: IRC Subchapter L Part I (§§801-818) / Form 1120-L
title: File U.S. Life Insurance Company Income Tax Return (Form 1120-L)
requirement: Each life insurance company in the group (taxed under IRC §801) must file Form 1120-L to report income, gains, losses, deductions, credits, and life-insurance-company taxable income, generally due by the 15th day of the 4th month after year-end. Pass = timely, accurate 1120-L filed (or included in a consolidated life/non-life return).
sourceNote: Verified IRS Form 1120-L instructions (2025) and 26 U.S.C. 801 (Subchapter L Part I). In force 2026.

regime: IRC Subchapter L Part II (§831) / Form 1120-PC
title: File U.S. Property & Casualty Insurance Company Income Tax Return (Form 1120-PC)
requirement: Each non-life (P&C) insurance company in the group, taxed under IRC §831, must file Form 1120-PC reporting income, deductions, and tax computed under §11, generally due by the 15th day of the 4th month after year-end. Pass = timely, accurate 1120-PC filed (or included in a consolidated return).
sourceNote: Verified 26 U.S.C. 831 (LII) and IRS Form 1120-PC. In force 2026.

title: Ensure life contracts satisfy the §7702 definitional (CVAT or GPT/cash-value corridor) test
requirement: Each life insurance contract the group issues must meet the IRC §7702 statutory definition of a life insurance contract—satisfying either the cash value accumulation test or the guideline premium/cash value corridor test—so policyholder inside build-up receives life-insurance tax treatment. Pass = ongoing §7702 compliance testing with correction of failures.
sourceNote: Verified 26 U.S.C. 7702 (LII); §7702(f)(10) interest rates amended by CAA 2021. In force 2026.

title: Apply the §7702A 7-pay test and identify/report modified endowment contracts
requirement: The group must apply the IRC §7702A 7-pay test to life contracts, classify contracts that fail as modified endowment contracts (MECs), and treat distributions/loans from MECs under the less-favorable income-first rules (with reporting to policyholders and the IRS). Pass = MEC testing performed and MEC status correctly determined and reported.
sourceNote: Verified 26 U.S.C. 7702A referenced in §7702 (LII) and IRS Rev. Rul. 2005-6. In force 2026.

title: Ensure LTC contracts/riders qualify under §7702B for favorable tax treatment
requirement: Long-term care insurance contracts and combination LTC riders on life/annuity contracts must meet the IRC §7702B requirements for qualified LTC insurance (covering only qualified LTC services, guaranteed renewable, no prohibited cash surrender value) so benefits receive tax-favored treatment. Pass = LTC contracts/riders designed and administered to §7702B standards.
sourceNote: Verified 26 U.S.C. 7702B (LII); §7702B(e) permits qualified LTC riders on life contracts. In force 2026.

title: File Form 8966 FATCA Report for cash-value insurance and annuity accounts
requirement: As an FFI issuing cash value insurance or annuity contracts, the group's insurers must identify and document U.S. accounts and file Form 8966 (FATCA Report) reporting specified U.S. account holders/holders' balances and income for cash-value/annuity contracts, generally due March 31 following the calendar year. Pass = timely, complete Form 8966 filings.
sourceNote: Verified IRS Form 8966 instructions (2025) and 26 CFR 1.1471-4/1.1471-5(b)(1)(iv). In force 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
title: File Form 5500 annual return/report for each ERISA employee benefit plan
requirement: As plan administrator, the group must file a Form 5500 series annual return/report with the DOL for each covered ERISA pension and welfare benefit plan it sponsors. Filing is due the last day of the seventh month after plan year-end (July 31 for calendar-year plans), unless extended. Pass condition is a timely, complete electronic EFAST2 filing with required schedules and audit where applicable.
sourceNote: Verified on DOL/EBSA Form 5500 page and 2024 instructions; in force, penalty up to $2,670/day (2024 inflation-adjusted).

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
title: Furnish Summary Annual Report to plan participants and beneficiaries
requirement: The plan administrator must furnish a Summary Annual Report (SAR) summarizing the Form 5500 to each participant and each beneficiary receiving benefits, within nine months after plan year-end (or two months after an extended Form 5500 deadline). Pension plans providing an annual funding notice are excepted. Pass condition is timely distribution in the prescribed content and delivery form.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 29 CFR 2520.104b-10; current, nine-month furnishing rule in force.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
title: Furnish Summary Plan Description to participants within statutory deadlines
requirement: The plan administrator must furnish each participant a Summary Plan Description within 90 days of becoming a participant (120 days for a new plan), an updated SPD every 5 years if amended (otherwise every 10 years), and provide plan documents on written request. Pass condition is a timely SPD written to be understood by the average participant containing the 29 CFR 2520.102-3 content.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 1022/1024(b) and 29 CFR 2520.102-3; 90/120-day and 5/10-year rules current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
title: Discharge ERISA fiduciary duties of loyalty and prudence over plan assets
requirement: Every named fiduciary and plan committee must discharge duties solely in the interest of participants and beneficiaries, for the exclusive purpose of providing benefits and defraying reasonable expenses, with the care, skill, prudence and diligence of a prudent expert, diversifying investments, and following plan documents. This is a continuing duty including ongoing monitoring of plan investments and service providers.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 1104(a) and eCFR 29 CFR 2550.404a-1; standard reaffirmed by Hughes v. Northwestern (2022).

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
title: Provide COBRA election notice to qualified beneficiaries after a qualifying event
requirement: As administrator of its group health plans, the group must notify qualified beneficiaries of their COBRA continuation rights: the employer notifies the administrator within 30 days of a qualifying event, and the administrator must furnish the election notice within 14 days, allowing a 60-day election period. Pass condition is timely, content-compliant election notices for each qualifying event.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 1166 and DOL COBRA employer guide; 30/14/60-day timelines current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor / HHS / IRS (tri-agency)
regime: ACA Summary of Benefits and Coverage
title: Distribute Summary of Benefits and Coverage to group health plan enrollees
requirement: The group health plan and its issuer must prepare and distribute a uniform Summary of Benefits and Coverage (SBC) with the uniform glossary and coverage examples to participants and beneficiaries at application, before enrollment/reenrollment, at renewal, and within 7 business days of a request. Pass condition is timely delivery of the standardized SBC; willful failure triggers a per-failure penalty.
sourceNote: Verified against 42 U.S.C. 300gg-15; SBC requirement current, penalty ~$1,443/failure (2026 inflation-adjusted).

title: File and pay annual PBGC premiums for covered defined benefit pension plans
requirement: For each PBGC-covered single-employer defined benefit plan it sponsors, the group must electronically file the annual premium filing via My PAA and pay the flat-rate per-participant premium plus, for single-employer plans, the variable-rate premium on unfunded vested benefits. Electronic filing is mandatory; failure is subject to penalty under ERISA section 4071.
sourceNote: Verified against PBGC 2026 Comprehensive Premium Filing Instructions and eCFR Part 4007; current.

title: File annual EEO-1 Component 1 workforce demographic report
requirement: As a private employer with 100 or more employees, the group must annually file the EEO-1 Component 1 report with the EEOC, reporting workforce headcount by job category, sex, and race/ethnicity based on a workforce snapshot pay period in the final quarter. Pass condition is a complete, timely electronic filing via the EEO-1 portal by the announced deadline.
sourceNote: Verified against EEOC EEO Data Collections page and 29 CFR 1602; annual collection current.

title: Refrain from employment discrimination based on protected characteristics
requirement: The group, as an employer of 15+ employees, must not discriminate in hiring, discharge, compensation, or terms and conditions of employment because of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity), or national origin, and must prevent and remedy unlawful harassment. Pass condition is nondiscriminatory employment practices; violations are enforceable via EEOC charge and litigation.
citation: 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2; Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
sourceNote: Verified against EEOC statute page; core Title VII prohibition in force (Bostock, 2020, confirmed sex includes SO/GI).

title: Provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities
requirement: As a covered employer (15+ employees), the group must not discriminate against a qualified individual on the basis of disability and must make reasonable accommodations to known limitations of applicants and employees unless doing so imposes undue hardship. Pass condition is a good-faith interactive process and provision of effective accommodations short of undue hardship.
sourceNote: Verified against 42 U.S.C. 12112 and EEOC reasonable-accommodation guidance; current.

title: Refrain from age discrimination against workers age 40 and older
requirement: As an employer with 20 or more employees, the group must not fail or refuse to hire, discharge, or otherwise discriminate in compensation, terms, or conditions of employment against any individual age 40 or older because of age. Pass condition is age-neutral employment practices across hiring, pay, promotion, layoff, and benefits.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 623 and EEOC ADEA page; 40+ protection and 20-employee threshold current.

title: Preserve personnel and employment records for the required retention period
requirement: The group must preserve personnel and employment records (applications, hiring, promotion, demotion, transfer, layoff, termination, pay, and accommodation requests) for at least one year from creation or the personnel action, one year from an involuntary termination, and until final disposition where a discrimination charge or action is pending. Pass condition is intact, retrievable records for the required period.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 29 CFR 1602.14; one-year and charge-pending retention rules current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division (WHD)
title: Pay federal minimum wage and overtime to covered nonexempt employees
requirement: The group must pay covered nonexempt employees at least the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hour and overtime at one-and-one-half times the regular rate for all hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Pass condition is correct wage and overtime payment for every workweek, subject to valid exemptions.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 206/207 and DOL WHD FLSA page; $7.25 federal floor (2009) still in force July 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division (WHD)
title: Maintain FLSA wage-and-hour records for covered employees
requirement: The group must make, keep, and preserve accurate records of each nonexempt employee's wages, hours worked, and conditions of employment, retaining payroll records for at least 3 years and supporting time and wage-computation records for at least 2 years. Pass condition is complete, accurate records available for WHD inspection.
sourceNote: Verified against DOL WHD Fact Sheet 21 and 29 CFR 516; 3-year/2-year retention current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division (WHD)
title: Provide FMLA leave and required eligibility and posting notices
requirement: As a covered employer (50+ employees in 20+ workweeks), the group must grant eligible employees up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave for qualifying reasons, post the FMLA general notice conspicuously, and provide individual eligibility, rights-and-responsibilities, and designation notices (eligibility notice within 5 business days of a leave request). Pass condition is granting leave and issuing the required notices on time.
sourceNote: Verified against 29 U.S.C. 2612/2619 and 29 CFR 825.300; 12-week entitlement and 5-day notice current.

title: Maintain OSHA 300 Log, 301 Incident Reports, and post 300A annual summary
requirement: For each establishment with 10+ employees not in a partially exempt industry, the group must record work-related injuries and illnesses on the OSHA Form 300 Log and Form 301 Incident Reports, complete and certify the Form 300A annual summary, post the 300A from February 1 to April 30, and retain the records for 5 years. Pass condition is accurate, contemporaneous records and timely posting.
sourceNote: Verified against OSHA recordkeeping pages and 29 CFR 1904; 10-employee threshold, 5-year retention, Feb1-Apr30 posting current.

title: Electronically submit injury and illness records to OSHA annually
requirement: Establishments with 250+ employees, and 20-249-employee establishments in designated industries, must electronically submit Form 300A data to OSHA by March 2 each year; establishments with 100+ employees in designated high-hazard industries must also submit detailed Form 300 and 301 data. Pass condition is timely electronic submission via the OSHA Injury Tracking Application.
sourceNote: Verified against OSHA final rule (eff. Jan 1, 2024) and 29 CFR 1904.41; March 2 deadline current.

title: Report work-related fatalities and severe injuries to OSHA within deadlines
requirement: The group must report to OSHA any work-related fatality within 8 hours, and any in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye within 24 hours of learning of it (fatality reportable if within 30 days of the incident; the others if within 24 hours of the incident). Pass condition is a timely report by phone or the online form for each qualifying event.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 29 CFR 1904.39; 8-hour fatality / 24-hour severe-injury reporting current.

title: Furnish a workplace free from recognized serious hazards (General Duty Clause)
requirement: The group must furnish to each employee a place of employment free from recognized hazards that are causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm, and comply with applicable OSHA standards. Pass condition is abatement of recognized serious hazards; enforceable by OSHA citation where no specific standard applies.
sourceNote: Verified against OSH Act sec. 5(a)(1) text on osha.gov; General Duty Clause in force.

title: Keep accurate books and records and maintain internal accounting controls (FCPA)
requirement: As an SEC issuer, the parent must make and keep books, records, and accounts that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect transactions and dispositions of assets, and devise and maintain a system of internal accounting controls sufficient to provide reasonable assurances over transaction authorization and asset access. Pass condition is accurate records and adequate controls, regardless of any foreign bribery.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. 78m(b)(2) and DOJ/SEC FCPA Resource Guide; issuer accounting provisions in force.

title: Refrain from corrupt payments to foreign officials (FCPA anti-bribery)
requirement: The group and its officers, directors, employees, and agents must not corruptly offer, pay, promise, or authorize payment of money or anything of value to a foreign official, directly or through intermediaries, to obtain or retain business or secure an improper advantage. Pass condition is no prohibited corrupt payments; maintaining an effective anti-corruption compliance program mitigates liability.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. 78dd-1 and DOJ FCPA Unit page; anti-bribery prohibition for issuers in force.

regulatorName: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) / DOJ Antitrust Division
title: File HSR premerger notification and observe the antitrust waiting period
requirement: For an acquisition of voting securities, assets, or interests exceeding the annually-adjusted HSR size thresholds, both parties must submit a premerger notification with documentary material to the FTC and DOJ, pay the filing fee, and observe the statutory waiting period (generally 30 days) before closing. Pass condition is a compliant filing and expired/terminated waiting period prior to consummation.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. 18a and FTC premerger rules; revised HSR form effective Feb 2025, thresholds adjusted annually.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division / FTC
title: Refrain from agreements in restraint of trade (Sherman Act Section 1)
requirement: The group must not enter into contracts, combinations, or conspiracies that unreasonably restrain trade, including price-fixing, bid-rigging, or market/customer allocation with competitors. The McCarran-Ferguson exemption does not shield boycott, coercion, or intimidation, nor conduct outside the 'business of insurance' or not regulated by state law. Pass condition is antitrust-compliant conduct; per se violations are criminally enforceable.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. 1 and McCarran-Ferguson 15 U.S.C. 1012-1013; boycott exception and 2021 health-insurance repeal noted.

title: Refrain from unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce (FTC Act Section 5)
requirement: The group must not engage in unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce: no material representations or omissions likely to mislead a reasonable consumer, and no practices causing substantial unavoidable consumer injury not outweighed by benefits. Pass condition is truthful, non-deceptive, and non-unfair conduct toward consumers, enforceable by FTC action.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. 45; note the insurance business is largely carved out under McCarran-Ferguson, so FTC UDAP reaches the group's non-insurance and general commercial conduct.

regulatorName: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority / national supervisory authorities
title: Maintain an effective system of governance with transparent structure and documented written policies
requirement: Every insurance and reinsurance undertaking must have in place an effective system of governance providing for sound and prudent management, with a transparent organisational structure, clear allocation and segregation of responsibilities, and written policies (at least on risk management, internal control, internal audit and, where relevant, outsourcing) reviewed at least annually and approved by the administrative, management or supervisory body (AMSB). It must be proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of operations.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex consolidated Solvency II Directive and EIOPA Single Rulebook; in force, as amended; current as of 2026 (Solvency II review applies from 30 Jan 2027).

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Ensure all key-function holders and those running the undertaking meet fit-and-proper requirements
requirement: The undertaking must ensure that all persons who effectively run the undertaking or hold other key functions are at all times fit (professional qualifications, knowledge and experience adequate for sound and prudent management) and proper (good repute and integrity), and must notify the supervisory authority of any change in the identity of such persons and provide the information needed to assess fitness and propriety.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 42 (fit and proper); in force as amended; current 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Operate a risk-management system covering underwriting, ALM, investment, liquidity, concentration and operational risk
requirement: The undertaking must have an effective risk-management system comprising strategies, processes and reporting procedures to continuously identify, measure, monitor, manage and report the risks it faces, covering at least underwriting and reserving, asset-liability management, investment (including derivatives), liquidity and concentration risk, operational risk, and reinsurance/risk-mitigation. Internal risk methodologies must not rely solely or automatically on external credit ratings.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 44 (risk management function/system); in force as amended; current 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Internal Model Risk-Management Duty (Art. 44(5))
title: For internal-model users, task the risk-management function with model design, testing and validation
requirement: Where the undertaking uses a full or partial internal model, the risk-management function must additionally design and implement the model, test and validate it, document the model and any subsequent changes, analyse its performance and produce summary reports, and inform the AMSB about the model's performance suggesting improvements.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 44(5); applies to internal-model undertakings; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Conduct and document a regular Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA)
requirement: As part of its risk-management system the undertaking must regularly (and immediately following any significant change in its risk profile) conduct an Own Risk and Solvency Assessment covering its overall solvency needs given its specific risk profile, continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical-provisions rules, and the significance of any deviation of its risk profile from the SCR standard-formula/internal-model assumptions. The ORSA must be integral to business strategy and taken into account in strategic decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 45 and EIOPA ORSA Guidelines; performed at least annually plus on material risk-profile change; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Submit the ORSA supervisory report to the supervisor after each assessment
requirement: Following each ORSA the undertaking must inform the supervisory authority of the results, submitting the ORSA supervisory report as part of information provided under Article 35. The report presents the qualitative and quantitative results of the assessment and the methods and assumptions used, and is due within two weeks of the AMSB concluding the assessment.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 45(6) and EIOPA Guidelines on ORSA; report submitted as part of Art. 35 reporting; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Maintain an internal control system including a compliance function
requirement: The undertaking must have an effective internal control system comprising administrative and accounting procedures, an internal control framework, appropriate reporting arrangements, and a compliance function that advises the AMSB on compliance with laws, regulations and administrative provisions, assesses the impact of legal-environment changes, and identifies and assesses compliance risk.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 46 (internal control and compliance function); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Operate an objective, independent internal audit function reporting findings to the AMSB
requirement: The undertaking must provide for an effective internal audit function evaluating the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control system and other elements of the system of governance. The function must be objective and independent from operational functions; its findings and recommendations must be reported to the AMSB, which determines and ensures the actions taken for each.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 47 (internal audit); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Operate an actuarial function coordinating technical provisions and issuing an annual actuarial report
requirement: The undertaking must provide for an effective actuarial function that coordinates the calculation of technical provisions, ensures appropriateness of methodologies, models and assumptions, assesses data sufficiency and quality, compares best estimates against experience, expresses an opinion on the overall underwriting policy and on the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements, and contributes to the risk-management system. The function must produce a written report to the AMSB at least annually documenting the tasks undertaken, results, and any deficiencies with remediation recommendations.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 48 and Delegated Reg. 2015/35 Art. 272 (actuarial function report); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Govern outsourcing so accountability is retained and notify supervisor before outsourcing critical functions
requirement: The undertaking remains fully responsible for discharging all obligations when outsourcing functions or activities, and must not outsource in a way that materially impairs the quality of governance, unduly increases operational risk, impairs the supervisor's ability to monitor, or undermines continuous service to policyholders. It must notify the supervisory authority in a timely manner prior to outsourcing critical or important functions/activities and of any subsequent material developments.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 49 (outsourcing); prior notification for critical/important functions; in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Invest all assets in accordance with the prudent person principle
requirement: The undertaking must invest all its assets in accordance with the prudent person principle: it may only invest in assets and instruments whose risks it can properly identify, measure, monitor, manage, control and report; all assets (particularly those covering the MCR and SCR) must be invested to ensure security, quality, liquidity and profitability of the whole portfolio; assets covering technical provisions must be invested appropriately to the nature and duration of the liabilities and in the best interest of policyholders; and derivatives are permissible only insofar as they reduce risk or facilitate efficient portfolio management.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 132 (prudent person principle); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Establish technical provisions as best estimate plus risk margin
requirement: The undertaking must establish technical provisions equal to the current amount it would have to pay to transfer its (re)insurance obligations to another undertaking, valued as the sum of a best estimate (probability-weighted average of future cash flows discounted using the relevant risk-free term structure) and a risk margin, calculated prudently, reliably and objectively using relevant market information and consistent with it.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 76-77 (technical provisions, best estimate + risk margin); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Classify own-fund items into Tiers 1, 2 and 3 by quality
requirement: The undertaking must classify each basic and ancillary own-fund item into one of three tiers according to whether it possesses the characteristics of permanent availability and subordination (and, for Tier 1, loss-absorbency and sufficient duration), determining the tier by reference to the extent to which the item meets these features regardless of its legal form.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 93-96 and EIOPA Guidelines on classification of own funds; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Eligible Own Funds Limits (Art. 98)
title: Hold eligible own funds within the tier limits to cover the SCR and MCR
requirement: The undertaking must ensure that eligible own funds covering the SCR satisfy the quantitative limits (Tier 1 at least one half of the SCR; Tier 3 below 15% of the SCR; Tier 2 plus Tier 3 not exceeding 50% of the SCR) and that eligible own funds covering the MCR satisfy their limits (Tier 1 at least 80% of the MCR; Tier 2 not exceeding 20% of the MCR).
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 98 / tier-eligibility limits; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Hold eligible own funds covering the SCR calibrated to 99.5% VaR over one year
requirement: The undertaking must hold eligible own funds at least equal to the Solvency Capital Requirement, calculated so that it corresponds to the Value-at-Risk of basic own funds subject to a confidence level of 99.5% over a one-year period, covering all quantifiable risks (at least non-life and life underwriting, health underwriting, market, credit and operational risk) on an ongoing basis.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 100-101 and EIOPA SCR standard-formula rulebook (99.5% VaR / one year); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Calculate the SCR at least annually and recalculate on material risk-profile change
requirement: The undertaking must calculate the Solvency Capital Requirement at least once a year, report the result to the supervisory authority, and monitor the amount of eligible own funds and the SCR on an ongoing basis. Where the risk profile deviates significantly from the assumptions underlying the last reported SCR, it must recalculate the SCR without delay.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 102 (SCR calculation frequency and recalculation); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Hold eligible basic own funds covering the MCR and calculate/report it quarterly
requirement: The undertaking must hold eligible basic own funds at least equal to the Minimum Capital Requirement, calculated as a linear function of specified variables subject to a floor of 25% and cap of 45% of the SCR and no lower than the absolute floor (currently EUR 2.7m non-life / EUR 4m life, or higher for certain lines). The MCR must be calculated at least quarterly and the results reported to the supervisory authority.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 128-129 (MCR, floor/cap and absolute floor); MCR reported quarterly; in force 2026 (absolute-floor amounts revised periodically).

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Notify supervisor and submit a recovery plan on SCR non-compliance
requirement: Where the undertaking observes that it no longer complies with the SCR, or that there is a risk of non-compliance within the following three months, it must immediately inform the supervisory authority and, within two months of observing non-compliance, submit a realistic recovery plan for approval, then re-establish eligible own funds or reduce its risk profile to restore SCR compliance within six months (extendable).
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 138 (non-compliance with SCR, recovery plan); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Notify supervisor and submit a short-term finance scheme on MCR non-compliance
requirement: Where the undertaking observes that it no longer complies with the MCR or that there is a risk of non-compliance within the following three months, it must immediately inform the supervisory authority and, within one month of observing non-compliance, submit a short-term realistic finance scheme for approval to restore eligible basic own funds to at least the MCR or reduce its risk profile within three months.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 139 (non-compliance with MCR, finance scheme); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Submit periodic quantitative reporting templates (QRTs) to the supervisory authority
requirement: The undertaking must submit to its supervisory authority the information necessary for supervision, structured in the harmonised quantitative reporting templates (QRTs) prescribed by the implementing technical standards, on a predefined periodic basis — annually and, for a defined subset, quarterly — covering balance sheet, own funds, SCR/MCR, technical provisions, assets and other prescribed content.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/894 (ITS on reporting templates, applicable from 31/12/2023); revised QRT set applies from Q1 2027; current 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Regular Supervisory Report (Art. 35 / Del. Reg. Art. 304-311)
title: Submit the narrative Regular Supervisory Report (RSR) to the supervisor
requirement: The undertaking must submit to its supervisory authority a narrative Regular Supervisory Report containing the information required for supervision, structured across the same sections as the SFCR (business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes, capital management) in greater detail, at least every three years in full (with an annual summary of material changes), or more frequently if required by the supervisor.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook (elements of regular supervisory reporting) and Delegated Reg. 2015/35 Arts. 304-311; full RSR at least triennially; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Publicly disclose an annual Solvency and Financial Condition Report (SFCR)
requirement: The undertaking must publicly disclose, at least annually, a Solvency and Financial Condition Report describing its business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes, and capital management (including SCR and MCR amounts). The report must be approved by the AMSB before publication and, following the 2024 review, is split into a part addressed to policyholders and beneficiaries and a part addressed to other market participants.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 51 (SFCR); split policyholder/other-stakeholder structure introduced by the 2024 amending Directive; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Obtain AMSB approval and observe non-disclosure limits for the SFCR
requirement: The undertaking must ensure the SFCR is approved by the AMSB and published only after that approval, and may only withhold information where disclosure would give competitors undue advantage or breach confidentiality obligations, with any such non-disclosure explained and permitted by the supervisor; it must also disclose promptly the nature and effects of any major development significantly affecting the SFCR's relevance.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 53-54 (SFCR non-disclosure limits, approval, updates); in force as amended 2026.

title: Disclose an annual group Solvency and Financial Condition Report
requirement: The participating insurance/reinsurance undertaking, insurance holding company or mixed financial holding company at group level must publicly disclose, at least annually, a Solvency and Financial Condition Report at the level of the group, either as a single SFCR covering the group and its subsidiaries or as a combined document, describing group business, governance, risk profile, valuation and capital management.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 256 (group SFCR); applies to the group parent; in force as amended 2026.

title: Calculate and hold group-level eligible own funds covering the group SCR
requirement: The group must calculate its group solvency (by default the accounting consolidation-based method) and ensure that eligible own funds available at group level are at least equal to the group Solvency Capital Requirement on an ongoing basis, with the group supervisor and the group parent monitoring compliance and applying the SCR-recovery provisions at group level where there is non-compliance.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Arts. 218-230 (group solvency, consolidation method); in force as amended 2026.

title: Apply system-of-governance and ORSA requirements at group level
requirement: The participating undertaking / holding company at the head of the group must ensure the system-of-governance requirements (risk management, internal control, key functions) apply mutatis mutandis at group level and must conduct a group ORSA assessing group-wide risks and overall solvency needs (which may, subject to supervisory agreement, be produced as a single document covering group and solo undertakings).
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 246 (group governance and group ORSA); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Obtain prior supervisory approval before using a full or partial internal model for the SCR
requirement: An undertaking wishing to calculate the SCR using a full or partial internal model instead of the standard formula must obtain prior approval from its supervisory authority, submitting a formal application with documentary evidence that the model satisfies the use test, statistical quality, calibration, validation and documentation standards (Arts. 120-125); the supervisor decides within six months of a complete application.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Art. 112 (approval of full/partial internal models); six-month decision period; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Internal Model Use Test (Art. 120)
title: Demonstrate the internal model is widely used in governance and decision-making (use test)
requirement: An undertaking using an internal model must demonstrate that the model is widely used in and plays an important role in its system of governance — in particular its risk-management system, decision-making processes, and economic and solvency capital assessment and allocation — and that the frequency of SCR calculation using the model is consistent with the frequency with which it is used for those other purposes.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 120 (use test); applies to internal-model undertakings; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Run a regular model validation cycle for the internal model
requirement: An undertaking using an internal model must have a regular cycle of model validation including monitoring the model's performance, reviewing the ongoing appropriateness of its specification, and testing its results against experience, using an effective statistical process for validating the model that demonstrates to the supervisor that the resulting capital requirements are appropriate.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 124 (validation standards); applies to internal-model undertakings; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Internal Model Change Policy (Art. 115)
title: Maintain an approved model-change policy and obtain approval for major model changes
requirement: An undertaking using an internal model must have a policy specifying minor and major changes to the model, approved by the supervisory authority as part of the model approval; major changes to the model, and changes to that change policy itself, are subject to prior supervisory approval, while minor changes are governed by the approved policy.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 115 (policy for changing full/partial internal models); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Data Quality for Internal Models (Art. 121)
title: Ensure accuracy, completeness and appropriateness of data used in the internal model
requirement: An undertaking using an internal model must base the probability distribution forecast on adequate, applicable and relevant actuarial and statistical techniques consistent with the methods used to calculate technical provisions, and must ensure that the data sets used are accurate, complete and appropriate, updating those data sets at least annually.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 121 (statistical quality standards / data quality); applies to internal-model undertakings; in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Remuneration Policy (Del. Reg. Art. 275)
title: Establish and apply a sound remuneration policy avoiding excessive risk-taking
requirement: As part of the system of governance the undertaking must establish, implement and maintain a written remuneration policy consistent with sound and effective risk management, avoiding incentives for excessive risk-taking, with a substantial portion of variable remuneration of AMSB members and key-function/risk-taking staff deferred and subject to performance/risk adjustment, overseen by a remuneration committee where proportionate.
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA Single Rulebook Delegated Reg. 2015/35 Art. 275 (remuneration policy), grounded in Dir. Art. 41(3); in force 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
regime: Solvency II — Valuation of Assets and Liabilities (Art. 75)
title: Value assets and liabilities on an economic, market-consistent basis
requirement: The undertaking must value assets at the amount for which they could be exchanged, and liabilities (other than technical provisions) at the amount for which they could be transferred or settled, between knowledgeable willing parties in an arm's length transaction, without adjustment for the undertaking's own credit standing — i.e. an economic, market-consistent Solvency II balance sheet.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 75 (valuation of assets and liabilities); in force as amended 2026.

regulatorName: National supervisory authorities under EIOPA framework
title: Comply with any supervisory capital add-on imposed on the SCR
requirement: Where the supervisory authority, following the supervisory review process, sets a capital add-on because the risk profile deviates significantly from the SCR assumptions or the system of governance deviates significantly from the standards, the undertaking must hold own funds covering the SCR as increased by that add-on and address the underlying deficiencies.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 37 (capital add-on); in force as amended 2026.

title: Measure insurance contract groups using fulfilment cash flows plus a contractual service margin (CSM)
requirement: The group must measure groups of insurance and reinsurance contracts at the risk-adjusted present value of future fulfilment cash flows plus a contractual service margin representing unearned profit, applying the general measurement model (or VFA/PAA where eligible), and release the CSM to profit or loss as insurance services are provided. Applies to all IFRS-reporting entities issuing insurance contracts.
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation standard page; IFRS 17 effective for annual periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2023 (replaced IFRS 4); in force July 2026.

title: Disclose reconciliations of insurance liability, CSM and risk adjustment movements each reporting period
requirement: The group must disclose, in its financial statements, reconciliations from opening to closing balances of the liability for remaining coverage, liability for incurred claims, and separately the estimates of present value of future cash flows, risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin, plus the effect of new contracts and expected CSM run-off. Required each annual reporting period.
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation standard page; disclosure requirements in force with IFRS 17 (periods from 1 Jan 2023).

title: Recognise expected credit losses on financial assets using the three-stage ECL impairment model
requirement: The group must recognise a loss allowance for expected credit losses on debt instruments measured at amortised cost or FVOCI, using 12-month ECL for performing assets (stage 1) and lifetime ECL where credit risk has significantly increased (stage 2) or the asset is credit-impaired (stage 3), updated at each reporting date with forward-looking information. Applies to all IFRS financial statements.
citation: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments, s.5.5 (impairment / expected credit losses)
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation standard page; IFRS 9 effective for annual periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2018 (replaced IAS 39); in force July 2026.

title: Classify and measure financial assets by business model and contractual cash-flow (SPPI) test
requirement: The group must classify each financial asset at amortised cost, fair value through OCI, or fair value through profit or loss based on the entity's business model for managing the asset and whether contractual cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest (SPPI), and measure it accordingly. Assessed at initial recognition and on business-model change.
citation: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments, ss.4.1-4.4 (classification and measurement)
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation standard page; in force since 1 Jan 2018.

title: Disclose material sustainability-related risks and opportunities affecting the entity (IFRS S1)
requirement: Where a jurisdiction adopts ISSB standards, the entity must disclose material information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably affect its cash flows, access to finance or cost of capital, across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets, in its general purpose financial reports. Effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024.
citation: IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation ISSB navigator; issued June 2023, effective for periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2024 (subject to jurisdictional adoption).

title: Disclose climate-related risks, opportunities and Scope 1/2/3 GHG emissions (IFRS S2)
requirement: Where a jurisdiction adopts ISSB standards, the entity must disclose climate-related risks and opportunities, including physical and transition risks, resilience/scenario analysis, and gross Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions measured per the GHG Protocol, in its sustainability disclosures. Effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024.
citation: IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures, paras 29-33 (metrics incl. GHG emissions)
sourceNote: Verified on IFRS Foundation ISSB navigator; issued June 2023, effective for periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2024.

title: Publish an ESRS sustainability statement in the management report (Wave 1 undertakings)
requirement: In-scope large EU undertakings and EU parents of large groups (Wave 1: large public-interest entities with over 500 employees) must include a dedicated sustainability statement in their management report, prepared under the European Sustainability Reporting Standards on a double-materiality basis. First applied to the 2024 financial year with reports published in 2025 and each year thereafter.
sourceNote: Verified on European Commission corporate sustainability reporting page; Wave 1 first reported FY2024 in 2025; Omnibus 'quick-fix' froze added requirements for FY2025-2026 but Wave 1 obligation remains in force July 2026.

title: Obtain limited assurance on the ESRS sustainability statement
requirement: In-scope undertakings must have their sustainability reporting subjected to a limited assurance engagement by a statutory auditor or independent assurance services provider, with an assurance opinion published alongside the sustainability statement. Applies annually for undertakings subject to CSRD sustainability reporting.
citation: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 (CSRD) amending Directive 2006/43/EC, Art 34(1) (assurance of sustainability reporting)
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex CSRD consolidated text; limited assurance requirement in force for Wave 1 from FY2024; European Commission to adopt limited-assurance standards.

title: Disclose the proportion of turnover, CapEx and OpEx that is Taxonomy-aligned
requirement: Undertakings subject to sustainability reporting must disclose, as part of their sustainability statement, the proportion of turnover, capital expenditure and operating expenditure associated with Taxonomy-eligible and Taxonomy-aligned environmentally sustainable economic activities, using the prescribed KPI templates. Reported annually.
citation: Regulation (EU) 2020/852, Art 8; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 (Disclosures Delegated Act)
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex Regulation 2020/852; Art 8 disclosures in force; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73 simplified/reduced data points from FY2025 (applying 1 Jan 2026).

title: Publish an entity-level principal adverse sustainability impacts (PAI) statement
requirement: As a financial market participant (via its asset-management/insurance-investment entities), the group must publish and maintain on its website a statement on how it considers principal adverse impacts of investment decisions on sustainability factors, using the mandatory PAI indicators, or explain why it does not, updated annually by 30 June for the preceding reference period.
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex Regulation 2019/2088; SFDR applies from 10 Mar 2021, RTS/PAI reporting from 1 Jan 2023 (first statements by 30 Jun 2023); in force July 2026.
