title: Provide Article 8/9 product sustainability disclosures (pre-contractual, website and periodic)
requirement: For each investment product marketed in the EU that promotes environmental/social characteristics (Art 8) or has sustainable investment as its objective (Art 9), the group must provide the prescribed sustainability disclosures in pre-contractual documents, on its website, and in annual periodic reports, using the mandatory RTS templates. Ongoing per product.
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex Regulation 2019/2088; product disclosures apply since 10 Mar 2021, periodic templates from 1 Jan 2023; category set as ESG-adjacent (best fit: sustainability disclosure).

regulatorName: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) / European Commission (PRIIPs)
title: Produce and provide a Key Information Document (KID) for each insurance-based investment product
requirement: As manufacturer of packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (e.g. unit-linked, index-linked and with-profits life products) sold to EU retail investors, the group must draw up a standardised max-3-page Key Information Document covering risks, costs and performance scenarios, publish it, keep it up to date, and ensure it is provided to retail investors in good time before they are bound.
sourceNote: Verified on European Commission PRIIPs page; PRIIPs Regulation applies from 1 Jan 2018; in force July 2026.

title: Rotate the statutory audit firm within the maximum PIE engagement tenure
requirement: As a public-interest entity, the group's EU statutory-audit engagements must not exceed the maximum durations set for PIEs (a base maximum of 10 years, extendable on public tender or joint audit), after which a cooling-off period applies before the same firm may be re-appointed. Enforced at each mandate renewal.
citation: Regulation (EU) No 537/2014, Art 17 (duration of the audit engagement)
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex Regulation 537/2014; in force since 17 Jun 2016; PIE audit-firm rotation applies July 2026.

title: Comply with the non-audit services prohibition and 70% fee cap for the statutory auditor
requirement: The group must not receive prohibited non-audit services from its EU statutory auditor, and must ensure that fees for permitted non-audit services (supplied for three or more consecutive years) do not exceed 70% of the average statutory audit fees of the prior three financial years, with permitted services pre-approved by the audit committee.
citation: Regulation (EU) No 537/2014, Art 4(2) (fee cap) & Art 5 (prohibited non-audit services)
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex Regulation 537/2014; NAS restrictions and 70% cap in force since 17 Jun 2016.

regulatorName: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
regime: EIOPA Guidelines on outsourcing to cloud service providers (EIOPA-BoS-20-002)
title: Maintain a register of cloud outsourcing arrangements and pre-notify critical/important outsourcing
requirement: Insurance and reinsurance undertakings must maintain an up-to-date register of all cloud outsourcing arrangements (distinguishing critical/important functions), make it available to the supervisor on request, conduct pre-outsourcing risk assessment and due diligence, and notify the national supervisory authority in a timely manner before outsourcing a critical or important operational function to a cloud service provider.
citation: EIOPA Guidelines on outsourcing to cloud service providers (EIOPA-BoS-20-002), Guidelines 4-8 & 10
sourceNote: Verified on EIOPA final guidelines PDF; apply to arrangements entered/amended from 1 Jan 2021, legacy arrangements to be reviewed by 31 Dec 2022; in force July 2026.

regulatorName: European Commission (Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive)
title: Conduct human-rights and environmental due diligence across the chain of activities (CSDDD, phased)
requirement: Very large in-scope companies must establish a risk-based due-diligence process to identify, prevent, mitigate and remediate adverse human-rights and environmental impacts in their own operations and chain of activities, and adopt a transition plan for climate-change mitigation. Post-Omnibus, the first wave applies from 26 July 2028 to companies with over 3,000 employees and over EUR 900m worldwide turnover.
citation: Directive (EU) 2024/1760 (CSDDD), Arts 5-16, as amended by Directives (EU) 2025/794 and (EU) 2026/470
sourceNote: Verified on European Commission CSDDD page; Directive in force 25 Jul 2024, Omnibus raised thresholds; first-wave application 26 Jul 2028, Art 16 reporting FY from 1 Jan 2029/2030 — future-dated as of July 2026.

regulatorName: Financial Conduct Authority / Prudential Regulation Authority (Bank of England)
regime: UK Operational Resilience (FCA PS21/3 / PRA PS6/21)
title: Identify important business services and set impact tolerances for each
requirement: The group's UK-regulated (re)insurance entities must identify their important business services, set an impact tolerance for the maximum tolerable disruption to each, and remain able to stay within those tolerances in severe-but-plausible scenarios; mapping, testing and required investments had to be completed by no later than 31 March 2025.
citation: FCA PS21/3 'Building operational resilience'; FCA SYSC 15A; PRA PS6/21 / SS1/21
sourceNote: Verified on FCA PS21/3 page; rules in force from 31 Mar 2022, full mapping/testing within impact tolerances required by 31 Mar 2025; in force July 2026.

regime: UK Critical Third Parties (PRA PS16/24 / FCA PS24/16)
title: Comply with the critical third parties oversight rules where designated by HM Treasury
requirement: Third parties providing systemic services to the UK financial sector, once designated as critical third parties by HM Treasury, must comply with the regulators' fundamental rules and operational-resilience/reporting requirements; regulated firms must factor the CTP regime into their third-party risk management. Rules took effect 1 January 2025 and apply on designation.
citation: PRA PS16/24 / FCA PS24/16 'Operational resilience: Critical third parties to the UK financial sector'; PRA SS6/24
sourceNote: Verified on FCA PS24/16 page; joint policy published 12 Nov 2024, rules effective 1 Jan 2025 (apply on HMT designation order); in force July 2026.

title: Apply customer due diligence to all EU business relationships under the AMLR
requirement: As an obliged financial entity, the group's EU insurers must identify and verify each customer and, for occasional transactions above thresholds, apply customer due diligence before establishing a business relationship, per AMLR Art. 19-20. Ongoing monitoring is required. Applies from 10 July 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; AMLR entered into force 9 July 2024, applies from 10 July 2027.

title: Appoint a management-body compliance manager and AML compliance officer
requirement: Under the AMLR the group's EU obliged entities must designate one member of the management body responsible for AML/CFT compliance and appoint a compliance officer, and maintain internal policies, controls and procedures proportionate to risk. Applies from 10 July 2027.
sourceNote: Verified via EUR-Lex and Norton Rose Fulbright analysis; internal governance/compliance-officer duties, application 10 July 2027.

title: Report suspicious transactions to the national Financial Intelligence Unit
requirement: The group's EU obliged entities must report to the competent FIU any suspicion that funds are proceeds of criminal activity or related to terrorist financing, and refrain from carrying out suspicious transactions, using the AMLA common reporting template. Applies from 10 July 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; AMLA to publish STR template by 10 July 2026, reporting applies from 10 July 2027.

title: Identify and verify beneficial owners of customers under AMLR transparency rules
requirement: The group's EU obliged entities must identify the beneficial owner(s) of customers that are legal entities or arrangements and verify their identity, applying harmonised transparency requirements including for non-EU entities with EU links. Applies from 10 July 2027.
citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR), Art. 22 & Ch. IV (Art. 51 et seq.)
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; beneficial-ownership transparency obligations, application 10 July 2027.

title: File and keep beneficial-ownership data current in Member State central registers
requirement: Under national laws transposing AMLD6, the group's EU legal entities must report beneficial-ownership information to the Member State central register and keep it accurate and up to date; registers are interconnected via the European Central Platform. Transposition deadline 10 July 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; central-register articles transpose by 10 July 2026, main directive by 10 July 2027.

title: Operate confidential internal whistleblowing reporting channels with follow-up
requirement: Each EU group entity with 50+ workers must establish secure, confidential internal reporting channels, acknowledge receipt within 7 days, designate an impartial person to follow up, and give the reporter feedback within 3 months. Ongoing since national transposition.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; in force, 50+ employee threshold transposed across Member States.

title: Report the gender pay gap and run a joint pay assessment where gap exceeds 5%
requirement: Under national laws transposing Directive 2023/970, EU employers with 100+ workers must report gender-pay-gap data to the competent authority (annually for 250+, every 3 years for 100-249) and, where an unjustified gap of 5%+ persists, conduct a joint pay assessment with worker representatives. First 250+ reports due June 2027.
sourceNote: Verified via EU Council; transposition deadline 7 June 2026, first large-employer reports by June 2027.

title: Implement cybersecurity risk-management measures for essential/important entities
requirement: Where in scope as an essential or important entity, the group's EU operations must adopt appropriate technical, operational and organisational cybersecurity risk-management measures (incident handling, business continuity, supply-chain security, encryption) with management-body accountability. In force via national transposition.
sourceNote: Verified via European Commission; NIS2 transposition deadline was 17 Oct 2024.

title: Report significant cyber incidents on the 24h / 72h / one-month timeline
requirement: On a significant incident the group's in-scope EU entity must submit an early warning to the CSIRT/competent authority within 24 hours, a fuller incident notification within 72 hours, and a final report within one month. Event-driven; in force via national transposition.
sourceNote: Verified via European Commission; staged 24h/72h/1-month reporting under Art. 23.

title: Make connected-product and related-service data available to users on request
requirement: As a data holder of connected products/related services (e.g. telematics, connected-home, IoT devices tied to insurance), the group must make the generated product and related-service data available to the user, and to third parties the user designates, readily and free of charge. Applies from 12 September 2025.
sourceNote: Verified via European Commission; Data Act applies from 12 Sept 2025.

title: Design connected products for data access by default (access-by-design)
requirement: Connected products the group places on the EU market (and related services) must be designed and manufactured so that product and related-service data are, by default, easily and securely accessible to the user in a structured, machine-readable format. Applies to products placed on the market after 12 September 2026.
sourceNote: Verified via European Commission; access-by-design duty applies to products placed on market after 12 Sept 2026.

title: Operate a product-approval process with a defined target market for each product
requirement: As a product manufacturer under the IDD, the group must maintain, operate and review a written product oversight and governance policy that specifies an identified target market, tests products against target-market needs, and takes corrective action for products detrimental to customers.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex/EIOPA rulebook; POG in force since IDD application 2018.

title: Provide a standardised Insurance Product Information Document for non-life products
requirement: Before concluding a non-life insurance contract, the group's distributors must give the customer a standardised, stand-alone Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) presenting the main features, cover, exclusions and obligations in a clear comparable format.
sourceNote: Verified via EIOPA; IPID required for non-life products since IDD application 2018.

title: Perform a demands-and-needs assessment before every insurance sale
requirement: Prior to concluding any insurance contract, the group's distributors must specify the customer's demands and needs based on information obtained and ensure the product proposed is consistent with them, to prevent mis-selling. Applies to all insurance contracts.
sourceNote: Verified via EIOPA rulebook; demands-and-needs test in force since IDD application 2018.

title: Complete at least 15 hours of professional training per year for distribution staff
requirement: The group's insurance distribution intermediaries and relevant employees must complete a minimum of 15 hours of continuing professional training or development per year, with the firm maintaining evidence of compliance.
sourceNote: Verified via EIOPA rulebook; 15-hour annual CPD minimum under IDD.

title: Provide a PRIIPs Key Information Document before selling insurance-based investment products
requirement: As manufacturer of insurance-based investment products (unit-linked / with-profits life), the group must draw up a PRIIPs Key Information Document (max 3 pages, standardised format covering risk, costs, performance) and ensure it is provided to the retail investor in good time before conclusion.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; KID rules in force since 1 Jan 2018 (Del. Reg. 2017/653).

title: Review and revise the PRIIPs KID at least every 12 months and on material change
requirement: The group as PRIIP manufacturer must regularly review the information in each KID, revise it whenever a change significantly affects it, and at least every twelve months while the product is offered, and publish the revised KID promptly.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and ESMA Q&A; 12-month/material-change KID review duty.

regulatorName: Serious Fraud Office / Ministry of Justice
title: Maintain adequate procedures to prevent bribery by associated persons
requirement: As a commercial organisation carrying on business in the UK, the group must have in place adequate anti-bribery procedures (proportionate, risk-assessed, with due diligence, training and monitoring) to defend against the strict-liability Section 7 offence of failing to prevent bribery by associated persons anywhere in the world.
sourceNote: Verified on legislation.gov.uk; s.7 offence with adequate-procedures defence, in force since 1 July 2011.

title: Conduct and submit an annual Own Risk and Solvency Assessment as an IAIG
requirement: Under the ERM framework required by ICP 16 and ComFrame, the group as an Internationally Active Insurance Group must perform an Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) assessing material risks and capital adequacy against its business plan, and submit it at least annually to the group-wide supervisor.
sourceNote: Verified via IAIS ICP Online Tool; ICPs/ComFrame updated Dec 2024, implementation from 2025.

title: IAIS ICP 16 (ERM) / ComFrame — Recovery Planning
requirement: As an IAIG, the group must develop and maintain a recovery plan (reviewed and updated) that identifies in advance credible options to restore its financial position and viability under severe stress, made available to the group-wide supervisor.
sourceNote: Verified via IAIS ICP Online Tool; recovery plans required for all IAIGs, updated material adopted Dec 2024.

title: Calculate and report the group-wide ICS as the IAIG prescribed capital requirement
requirement: As an IAIG, the group must calculate a consolidated group-wide capital position against the Insurance Capital Standard — the ComFrame Prescribed Capital Requirement — and report it to the group-wide supervisor as jurisdictions implement the standard adopted for reference from 1 January 2025.
citation: IAIS Insurance Capital Standard (adopted Dec 2024), ComFrame
sourceNote: Verified via IAIS; ICS adopted Dec 2024 as group PCR for IAIGs, reference from 1 Jan 2025, jurisdictional implementation phasing in.

regime: IAIS Holistic Framework for systemic risk
title: Provide data for annual IAIS Global Monitoring Exercise systemic-risk assessment
requirement: As a large internationally active insurer, the group is subject to the IAIS Holistic Framework and must supply data supporting the annual Global Monitoring Exercise through which supervisors assess sector-wide and individual-insurer systemic risk and apply supervisory responses.
citation: IAIS Holistic Framework for the assessment and mitigation of systemic risk
sourceNote: Verified via IAIS; Holistic Framework operational since 2020, annual Global Monitoring Exercise.

title: Apply a risk-based AML/CFT approach with CDD across group operations
requirement: As a financial institution, the group's operations in FATF-member jurisdictions must (via national law) apply a risk-based approach — customer identification and verification, beneficial-ownership CDD, ongoing monitoring and record-keeping — reflecting FATF Recommendation 1 and Recommendation 10.
sourceNote: Verified via FATF; global AML/CFT standard implemented through national law.

title: Report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit
requirement: Under FATF Recommendation 20, as implemented in national law, the group's financial-institution entities must promptly report to the national FIU any suspicion that funds are the proceeds of crime or linked to terrorist financing, regardless of transaction size.
sourceNote: Verified via FATF; STR obligation under R.20, implemented through national law.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, Model #900)
regime: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act (Model #900)
title: Acknowledge claim communications with reasonable promptness
requirement: An insurer must acknowledge and act with reasonable promptness on pertinent communications regarding claims arising under its policies (Model #900 Sec. 4.B). Failing to do so, when done flagrantly or as a general business practice, is an unfair claims practice subject to cease-and-desist and monetary penalties. Applies to personal and commercial claims (excludes workers' comp, fidelity, surety, boiler & machinery).
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #900 (adopted 1990, amended/reprinted 1991); in force as adopted by states as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, Model #900)
regime: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act (Model #900)
title: Adopt and implement reasonable standards for prompt claim investigation
requirement: An insurer must adopt and implement reasonable standards for the prompt investigation and settlement of claims arising under its policies (Model #900 Sec. 4.C). Failure, if flagrant or a general business practice, constitutes an unfair claims practice. Covers personal and commercial claims.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #900; in force as adopted by states as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, Model #900)
regime: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act (Model #900)
title: Provide reasonable, accurate explanation of claim denial or compromise
requirement: On denying a claim or offering a compromise settlement, an insurer must promptly provide a reasonable and accurate explanation of the basis for that action (Model #900 Sec. 4.L). Failing to do so, if flagrant or a general business practice, is an unfair claims practice. Applies to personal and commercial claims.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #900; in force as adopted by states as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, Model #900)
regime: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act (Model #900)
title: Furnish necessary claim forms within 15 calendar days of request
requirement: An insurer must provide the forms necessary to present claims, with reasonable explanations regarding their use, within fifteen (15) calendar days of a request (Model #900 Sec. 4.M). Failure, if flagrant or a general business practice, is an unfair claims practice. Applies to personal and commercial claims.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #900; 15-day form-provision standard confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, Model #900)
regime: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act (Model #900)
title: Attempt good-faith prompt fair settlement where liability is clear
requirement: An insurer must attempt in good faith to effectuate prompt, fair and equitable settlement of claims in which liability has become reasonably clear (Model #900 Sec. 4.D), and must not compel insureds to sue by offering substantially less than amounts ultimately recovered (Sec. 4.E). Violations, if flagrant or a general business practice, are unfair claims practices. Personal and commercial claims.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #900; in force as adopted by states as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Trade Practices Act, Model #880)
title: Maintain a complete record of consumer complaints
requirement: An insurer must maintain a complete record of the complaints it has received; failure to maintain such complaint-handling records is a defined unfair trade practice under Model #880. The record must indicate the total number of complaints, their classification by line of insurance, the nature of each complaint, disposition, and time of processing. Applies to personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #880 (Unfair Trade Practices Act), Section 4 (failure to maintain complaint record)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #880 (amended 2020 rebating, 2024 lead-generator amendments); complaint-record duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Unfair Trade Practices Act, Model #880)
title: Refrain from misrepresentation and false advertising of insurance
requirement: An insurer and persons in the business of insurance must not misrepresent policy terms/benefits, issue false or misleading advertisements, or disseminate false information about an insurer or policy in any medium including email, internet or electronic posting (Model #880 Sec. 4, as amended 2024). Such acts are prohibited unfair trade practices. Applies to personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #880 (Unfair Trade Practices Act), Section 4.A-B
sourceNote: Verified via Model #880; 2024 amendments extended Sec. 4.B to email/internet/electronic advertising, confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act, Model #218)
title: Notify commissioner of producer termination for cause within 30 days
requirement: An insurer that terminates a producer's appointment, employment or contract for a reason set forth in Section 12 (or on knowledge the producer engaged in such conduct) must notify the insurance commissioner within 30 days of the effective date, in the prescribed format, and provide additional documentation on request (Model #218 Sec. 15). Enterprise-wide producer-distribution obligation across personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #218, Section 15 (Notification to Commissioner of Termination)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #218 (adopted 2000, amended 2000 and 2005); 30-day for-cause termination reporting confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act, Model #218)
title: Notify commissioner of producer termination without cause within 30 days
requirement: An insurer that terminates a producer's appointment, employment or contract for any reason not set forth in Section 12 must still notify the commissioner within 30 days of the effective date in the prescribed format (Model #218 Sec. 15). Enterprise-wide producer-distribution obligation; personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified via Model #218; 30-day no-cause termination notice confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act, Model #218)
title: Do not pay commissions to unlicensed persons for insurance transactions
requirement: An insurer or producer must not pay a commission, service fee, brokerage or other valuable consideration to any person for selling, soliciting or negotiating insurance if that person is required to be licensed under the Act and is not so licensed (Model #218 Sec. 13). Enterprise-wide; personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified via Model #218; unlicensed-compensation prohibition confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act, Model #680)
regime: NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act (Model #680)
title: Maintain antifraud initiatives to detect and prevent insurance fraud
requirement: An insurer must have antifraud initiatives reasonably calculated to detect, prosecute and prevent fraudulent insurance acts, which may include fraud investigators (employees or contractors) and/or an antifraud plan submitted to the commissioner (Model #680 Sec. 11). This underpins the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) function. Enterprise-wide across personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #680 (adopted 1995, amended through 2003); antifraud-initiative duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act, Model #680)
regime: NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act (Model #680)
title: Report suspected fraudulent insurance acts to the commissioner
requirement: A person engaged in the business of insurance who has knowledge or a reasonable belief that a fraudulent insurance act is being, will be, or has been committed must provide the commissioner the required information in the prescribed manner (Model #680 Sec. 6.A). Mandatory reporting; enterprise-wide across personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #680; mandatory fraud-reporting duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act, Model #680)
regime: NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act (Model #680)
title: Include fraud-warning statement on claim forms and applications
requirement: Every claim form and application for insurance (regardless of transmission form) must contain the prescribed fraud-warning statement that presenting a false claim or false application information is a crime subject to fines and imprisonment (Model #680 Sec. 4.A). Reinsurance claim forms/applications are exempt (Sec. 4.D). Applies to personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #680; mandatory fraud-warning on forms confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation, Model #570)
regime: NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation (Model #570)
title: Maintain advertising file of life/annuity ads for five years
requirement: An insurer must maintain at its home or principal office a complete file with a specimen of every life/annuity advertisement disseminated in the state (individual policies, plus typical blanket/franchise/group ads), noting manner and extent of distribution and policy form number, subject to department inspection. Each advertisement must be kept for 5 years after discontinuance of use (Model #570 Sec. 9.A).
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #570 (amended 2015); 5-year advertising-file retention confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation, Model #570)
regime: NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation (Model #570)
title: File annual advertising certificate of compliance with commissioner
requirement: Each insurer subject to Model #570 must file with the commissioner, together with its annual statement, a certificate of compliance executed by an authorized officer stating that to the best of their knowledge the life/annuity advertisements disseminated in the state during the preceding statement year complied with the regulation and state insurance laws (Model #570 Sec. 9.C).
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #570; annual certificate-of-compliance filing confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation, Model #570)
regime: NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation (Model #570)
title: Maintain a system of control over all life/annuity advertisements
requirement: An insurer must establish and at all times maintain a system of control over the content, form and method of dissemination of all advertisements of its policies, including at least annual notification to agents, brokers and others authorized to disseminate ads of the prior-approval requirement and the most serious consequence of not obtaining approval (Model #570 Sec. 3.B).
sourceNote: Verified full text of Model #570; advertising system-of-control duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Rules Governing Advertisements of Accident and Sickness Insurance, Model #40)
regime: NAIC Advertisements of Accident and Sickness Insurance Model Regulation (Model #40)
title: Maintain accident-and-sickness advertising file for four years
requirement: An insurer must maintain at its home or principal office a complete file of all accident and sickness (health) advertisements, with a notation of manner and extent of distribution and the form number of any policy advertised, subject to inspection; each advertisement must be kept for at least 4 years after discontinuance of use (Model #40). Applies to individual, group and blanket A&H insurance.
citation: NAIC Model #40 (Rules Governing the Advertising of Accident and Sickness Insurance), advertising-file section
sourceNote: Verified via Model #40 official PDF; 4-year A&H advertising-file retention confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation, Model #672)
regime: NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation (Model #672)
title: Provide initial and annual privacy notices to consumers/customers
requirement: A licensee must provide a clear and conspicuous notice of its privacy policies and practices to a customer no later than when it establishes the customer relationship, and must provide the privacy notice at least annually during the continuation of the customer relationship (Model #672 Art. IV). Applies to nonpublic personal financial information across personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #672, Article IV (Privacy and Opt Out Notices for Financial Information)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #672 official PDF; initial and annual privacy-notice duty confirmed as of 2026 (Model #672 revision ongoing but not yet superseded).

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation, Model #672)
regime: NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation (Model #672)
title: Provide opt-out notice before disclosing financial info to third parties
requirement: Before disclosing nonpublic personal financial information to a nonaffiliated third party, a licensee must provide a clear opt-out notice explaining the consumer's right to opt out and a reasonable means to do so, and must honor an opt-out direction as soon as reasonably practicable (Model #672 Art. IV). Applies to personal and commercial lines.
sourceNote: Verified via Model #672 official PDF; financial-information opt-out duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation, Model #672)
regime: NAIC Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information Regulation (Model #672)
title: Obtain authorization before disclosing nonpublic personal health information
requirement: A licensee must not disclose nonpublic personal health information about a consumer or customer unless it obtains a valid authorization from the individual, subject to limited exceptions for insurance functions (Model #672 Art. VI). This is an opt-in standard distinct from the financial-information opt-out. Applies to personal and commercial lines handling health data.
citation: NAIC Model #672, Article VI (Rules for Health Information)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #672 official PDF; health-information authorization (opt-in) requirement confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Model Act, Model #670)
regime: NAIC Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Model Act (Model #670)
title: Provide notice of information practices to applicants and policyholders
requirement: An insurance institution or agent must provide a notice of information practices to applicants and policyholders no later than policy delivery (where info was collected only from the applicant or public records) or at initiation of collection (where info is collected from other sources), and by renewal date on renewals unless a compliant notice was given within the preceding 24 months (Model #670). Applies to personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #670, Section 4 (Notice of Insurance Information Practices)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #670 official PDF; notice-of-information-practices timing confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Model Act, Model #670)
regime: NAIC Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Model Act (Model #670)
title: Give reasons and access on adverse underwriting decisions
requirement: On an adverse underwriting decision, an insurance institution or agent must give the applicant/policyholder written notice of the specific reason(s), the sources of information supporting the decision, and the individual's right to access and correct recorded personal information (Model #670). Applies to personal and commercial lines.
citation: NAIC Model #670, Section 10 (Reasons for Adverse Underwriting Decisions)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #670 official PDF; adverse-underwriting-decision reason/access duty confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation, Model #275)
regime: NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation (Model #275, 2020 best-interest amendments)
title: Satisfy the four best-interest obligations on annuity recommendations
requirement: When recommending an annuity, a producer (and insurer where no producer is involved) must act in the consumer's best interest by satisfying four obligations: care, disclosure, conflict-of-interest, and documentation (Model #275 Sec. 6, 2020 amendments). The consumer's interest must be placed ahead of the producer's/insurer's financial interest. Applies to personal and commercial annuity sales.
citation: NAIC Model #275, Section 6 (Duties of Insurers and Insurance Producers)
sourceNote: Verified via Model #275 (2020 best-interest revision); four-obligation best-interest standard; adopted by most states by 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation, Model #275)
regime: NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation (Model #275, 2020 best-interest amendments)
title: Complete best-interest annuity producer training before soliciting
requirement: A producer must complete a one-time four-hour best-interest general annuity training course (or, for those who previously met prior suitability training, a one-hour update course generally within six months of the amended regulation's effective date) before selling or soliciting annuities, plus product-specific training (Model #275 Sec. 7). Applies to personal and commercial annuity sales.
sourceNote: Verified via Model #275 (2020 revision); 4-hour best-interest training + 1-hour update confirmed as of 2026.

regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation, Model #275)
regime: NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation (Model #275, 2020 best-interest amendments)
title: Maintain a supervision system reviewing annuity recommendations
requirement: An insurer must establish and maintain a supervision system reasonably designed to achieve compliance with Model #275, including procedures to review each annuity recommendation before issuance to ensure a reasonable basis that it effectively addresses the consumer's financial situation, needs and objectives (Model #275 Sec. 6.C). Applies to personal and commercial annuity business.
sourceNote: Verified via Model #275 (2020 revision); insurer supervision-system duty confirmed as of 2026.

regime: CA Earthquake Mandatory Offer (Ins. Code Ch. 8.5)
title: Offer earthquake coverage to every residential property policyholder (mandatory offer)
requirement: An insurer writing residential property insurance in California may not issue, deliver, or initially renew a policy unless the named insured is offered coverage for loss caused by earthquake. The offer may be made prior to, concurrent with, or within 60 days after issuance/renewal, and must be re-offered on an every-other-year basis if declined.
sourceNote: Verified on California Legislature leginfo; Chapter 8.5 in force, mandatory-offer requirement current as of 2026.

regime: CA Earthquake Mandatory Offer (Ins. Code Ch. 8.5)
title: Include commissioner-approved earthquake coverage disclosure/summary in the mandatory offer
requirement: When making the mandatory earthquake offer, the insurer must include prescribed disclosure language stating that residential property insurance does not cover earthquake damage and that earthquake coverage differs from and is typically more limited than homeowners coverage; CEA offers must carry a 14-point boldface CEA/CIGA disclosure. The summary form must be approved by the Commissioner.
sourceNote: Verified via California Insurance Code §§10082-10083 (leginfo/FindLaw); disclosure content current 2026.

regime: CA FAIR Plan (Ins. Code § 10091 et seq.)
title: Participate in and fund the California FAIR Plan as a writer of basic property insurance
requirement: Every insurer licensed to write and actually writing basic property insurance in California is a mandatory member of the California FAIR Plan Association and must share, in proportion to its market participation, in the equitable apportionment of basic property insurance and the Plan's obligations for last-resort coverage.
sourceNote: Verified via CA Ins. Code §10091 and CDI FAIR Plan page; mandatory membership current 2026.

title: File private flood insurance forms/rates and provide the NFIP-coverage-comparison disclosure
requirement: An insurer writing personal residential private flood insurance in Florida must make required flood filings with OIR, and standard/preferred/customized coverage must be at least as broad as NFIP; the insurer must give the insured a disclosure describing how the private flood coverage compares to a standard NFIP policy so consumers understand coverage differences.
sourceNote: Verified on Florida Legislature Online Sunshine; §627.715 in force, informational-rate option sunset Oct 1 2025.

title: Ensure private flood policies meet the federal 'private flood insurance' definition for mortgage acceptance
requirement: An insurer writing private residential flood insurance whose policy is to satisfy federally-related mortgage flood-coverage requirements must ensure the policy meets the statutory definition of private flood insurance so lenders must accept it in lieu of an NFIP Standard Flood Insurance Policy, and file forms/rates with TDI as required.
sourceNote: Federal private-flood definition verified via Congress.gov CRS IN10450; TDI form/rate filing regime current 2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Pet Insurance Model Act)
title: Provide pet insurance disclosures (preexisting conditions, waiting periods, exam requirements) and a free-look
requirement: In states that have adopted the Pet Insurance Model Act, an insurer writing pet insurance must disclose to consumers policy limitations including preexisting-condition and hereditary-condition exclusions, waiting/affiliation periods, and any exam requirements, and must provide a free-look/summary-of-terms; producers selling pet insurance must complete a training program.
citation: NAIC Model 633; e.g., Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 24-A, Ch. 39-A
sourceNote: Model 633 adopted by NAIC Aug 2022; verified on content.naic.org; enacted in ME, MS, LA, MD, HI and others as of 2025-2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Title Insurers Model Act)
title: Maintain title-insurance escrow/settlement accounts under required conditions
requirement: A title insurer (or its agent) acting as escrow, settlement, or closing agent must maintain escrow, settlement, and security-deposit funds in separate fiduciary accounts, keep those funds segregated from operating funds, and comply with statutory conditions on their handling to protect consumer closing funds.
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 628; escrow-account conditions adopted in substantially similar form across many states as of 2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Title Insurers Model Act)
title: Issue closing protection letters covering agent theft/fraud in real-estate closings
requirement: In adopting states, a title insurer must offer/issue a closing protection letter (CPL) to protect the insured and lender against loss of settlement funds due to the closing agent's fraud, dishonesty, or failure to comply with written closing instructions, subject to filed CPL forms and any prescribed charge.
citation: NAIC Model 628; state title CPL statutes/regs
sourceNote: CPL framework and 2021 NAIC fraud/CPL revisions verified on content.naic.org title-insurance topic page; current 2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model)
regime: NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act (Model 360)
title: Refund unearned credit insurance premium on early termination of the credit transaction
requirement: For credit life and credit accident-and-health insurance sold with a loan or credit transaction, when the coverage terminates before scheduled maturity the insurer must pay or credit to the debtor a refund of all unearned premium or unearned insurance charges, computed by a filed method (e.g., Rule of 78's or pro rata).
citation: NAIC Model 360 (Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act)
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 360 / companion regulation 370; unearned-premium refund duty current and widely adopted 2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Regulation)
regime: NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model Regulation (Model 370)
title: File credit insurance rates against the prima facie / loss-ratio rate standards
requirement: An insurer writing consumer credit insurance must file its credit life and credit A&H rates with the state and demonstrate they do not exceed the prima facie rates or otherwise meet the required loss-ratio standard; rates exceeding presumptive levels require actuarial justification and deviation approval.
citation: NAIC Model 370 (Consumer Credit Insurance Model Regulation)
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 370 (MO370.pdf); prima facie rate / loss-ratio standard current 2026.

regime: FL Warranty Associations - Motor Vehicle Service Agreements (Ch. 634 Part I)
title: License and maintain as a motor vehicle service agreement company
requirement: A company selling motor vehicle service agreements (extended vehicle service contracts) in Florida must obtain and maintain a license from OIR under Chapter 634 Part I, meet financial/net-asset and reserve requirements, file forms and rates, and is exempt from other Insurance Code provisions except as stated; fronting is prohibited.
sourceNote: Verified on Florida Senate Chapter 634 Part I; motor vehicle service agreement licensing in force 2026 (rule 69O-200).

regime: FL Warranty Associations - Service Warranty (Ch. 634 Part III)
title: License as a service warranty association and maintain minimum net assets
requirement: A service warranty association (covering consumer products such as appliances/electronics) in Florida must obtain a license from OIR under Chapter 634 Part III, file a verified financial statement, and have and maintain minimum net assets of $500,000 (with a limited 5-year phase-in for smaller, long-licensed, complaint-free companies).
sourceNote: Verified on Florida Senate Chapter 634 Part III; $500k net-asset and license requirements current 2026.

regime: CA Motor Clubs (Ins. Code Part 5, § 12140 et seq.)
title: Obtain a Certificate of Authority and meet net-worth minimum to operate an automobile/motor club
requirement: A motor club (auto club) selling or offering motor club service in California must obtain a Certificate of Authority from the Department of Insurance, and must maintain net worth of not less than $250,000 (total assets over total liabilities) as a condition of authority.
sourceNote: Verified on CDI motor-club application page and CA Ins. Code §§12142/12162.5; $250k net worth requirement current 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Workers' Compensation Board / Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Paid Family Leave (Workers' Comp Law Art. 9) / DBL
title: Provide statutory Paid Family Leave coverage as a mandatory rider on DBL disability policies
requirement: An insurer writing New York statutory disability benefits (DBL) coverage must provide Paid Family Leave coverage as a mandatory rider to each DBL policy, collect the DFS-set employee contribution (0.432% of wages, capped at $411.91 for 2026), and pay PFL benefits up to the 2026 maximum weekly benefit ($1,228.53) per the state schedule.
citation: N.Y. Workers' Comp. Law Art. 9 (§§ 200-242); 12 NYCRR Pt. 380
sourceNote: 2026 rate/benefit set by NY DFS; verified on paidfamilyleave.ny.gov and wcb.ny.gov; PFL-rider-on-DBL structure current 2026.

regulatorName: Colorado Division of Insurance / FAMLI Division
regime: Colorado FAMLI - Fully Insured Private Plans
title: File FAMLI private-plan policies with the Division of Insurance for approval before employer use
requirement: An insurance carrier offering a fully-insured Colorado Paid Family and Medical Leave (FAMLI) private plan must file its policy forms with the Colorado Division of Insurance and obtain state approval before the plan can be added to My FAMLI+ and used by employers; benefits must meet or exceed the state program (including the 2026 NICU additional-leave enhancement).
citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 8-13.3-501 et seq.; 3 CCR 702-4
sourceNote: Verified on Colorado DOI and famli.colorado.gov; carrier form-filing/approval and 2026 rate (0.88%) current.

regime: Maine Pet Insurance Act (2022, based on NAIC Model 633)
title: Comply with Maine pet insurance disclosure, waiting-period and producer-training requirements
requirement: An insurer writing pet insurance in Maine must comply with the Maine Pet Insurance Act (effective Jan 1, 2023), including consumer disclosures of preexisting-condition/hereditary exclusions and waiting periods, use of a summary of policy terms, and completion of a pet-insurance producer training program before selling.
sourceNote: Maine adoption of Model 633 effective 1/1/2023 confirmed via NAIC state-adoption page ST-633-1; in force 2026.

regulatorName: State Insurance Regulators (per NAIC Title Insurance Agent Model Act)
regime: NAIC Title Insurance Agent Model Act (Model 230)
title: License and appoint title insurance agents authorized to determine insurability and issue policies
requirement: A title insurer must ensure that persons performing title agent functions (searching/examining title, determining insurability, issuing title commitments/policies, and handling settlement) are licensed as title insurance agents and appointed by the insurer under the state's Title Insurance Agent Model Act, and must supervise those agents.
citation: NAIC Model 230 (Title Insurance Agent Model Act)
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 230; title-agent licensing/appointment framework adopted across states, current 2026.

regime: FL Warranty Associations - Home Warranty (Ch. 634 Part II)
title: License as a home warranty association and file forms/rates for home warranty contracts
requirement: A home warranty association issuing home warranty contracts (covering structural components/systems of residential property) in Florida must obtain a license from OIR under Chapter 634 Part II, meet the applicable financial/reserve requirements, and file its contract forms and rates for the office's review.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes Chapter 634 Part II (Home Warranty Associations); licensing regime in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (Model 630)
title: Mortgage guaranty insurer must establish and fund a statutory contingency reserve
requirement: A mortgage guaranty insurer must establish a contingency reserve out of net premium remaining after the unearned premium reserve, contributing an amount equal to 50% of remaining earned premium. Each calendar year's contribution must be held for 120 months; releases require actual incurred losses exceeding 35% of earned premium and prior commissioner approval.
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 630 (comprehensive revision adopted 2023); a state-adopted model, in force where enacted as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (Model 630)
title: Mortgage guaranty insurer must not exceed 25:1 aggregate risk-in-force to capital
requirement: A mortgage guaranty insurer whose total liability risk in force exceeds 25 times its capital, surplus and contingency reserve must cease writing new mortgage guaranty business until its risk in force is brought back within the 25-to-1 limit. Exceeding the limit is a State Regulatory Mortgage Insurer Capital Standard action-level event.
citation: NAIC Model 630, Section 6 (Limitation on Risk); SRMICS
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model 630 clean version on content.naic.org; 25:1 risk-to-capital retained in modern SRMICS framework as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (Model 630)
title: Mortgage guaranty insurance must be written on a monoline basis
requirement: A company transacting mortgage guaranty insurance must be a monoline insurer that writes only mortgage guaranty (and permitted authorized) insurance and no other kinds of insurance. This confines the risk and preserves the dedicated capital and contingency reserves for mortgage-credit exposure.
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org Model 630; monoline restriction is a core structural requirement in force where adopted as of 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Insurance Law Article 69 (Financial Guaranty Insurance Corporations)
title: Financial guaranty insurer must establish and maintain contingency reserves by category
requirement: A financial guaranty insurance corporation must establish and maintain contingency reserves to protect insureds against excessive losses in adverse economic cycles. The reserve is the greater of 50% of premiums written per category or prescribed percentages of principal guaranteed (0.55% for municipal bonds up to 2.5% for certain obligations), and may be net of collateral and qualifying reinsurance.
citation: N.Y. Ins. Law § 6903 (Contingency, Loss and Unearned Premium Reserves)
sourceNote: Verified against NY Senate consolidated laws ISC 6903 (2025 laws); in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Insurance Law Article 69 (Financial Guaranty Insurance Corporations)
title: Financial guaranty insurer must observe single-risk and aggregate exposure limits
requirement: A financial guaranty insurer must limit loss exposure on any single risk (net of collateral and reinsurance) - e.g. insured average annual debt service on a single municipal entity/revenue source may not exceed 10% of surplus to policyholders plus contingency reserve - and must maintain aggregate surplus and contingency reserves no less than prescribed fractions (e.g. 1/300th of net municipal liability) of guaranteed liabilities.
sourceNote: Verified against NY Ins. Law Article 69 § 6904 (2025 laws); single-risk and aggregate limits in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Insurance Law Article 69 (Financial Guaranty Insurance Corporations)
title: Financial guaranty insurance must be written only by a monoline corporation
requirement: Financial guaranty insurance may be transacted only by a monoline financial guaranty insurance corporation that writes no other kinds of insurance except permitted residual value, surety and credit insurance. A multiline insurer may not write financial guaranty coverage.
citation: N.Y. Ins. Law Article 69 (§ 6902 et seq., monoline requirement)
sourceNote: Verified against NY Senate Article 69; monoline confinement of financial guaranty in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Federal Insurance Office (Terrorism Risk Insurance Program)
regime: Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA), 15 U.S.C. 6701 note; 31 CFR Part 50
title: Insurer must make terrorism coverage available on commercial P&C policies
requirement: Each insurer writing commercial property and casualty lines subject to TRIA must make available coverage for insured losses from certified acts of terrorism that does not differ materially in terms, amounts, or limitations from coverage for other perils. Availability must be offered at policy issuance and renewal; the insured need not purchase it.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR Part 50 and Treasury TRIP page; Program authorized through Dec 31, 2027 (2019 reauthorization), extension to 2034 pending in Senate as of July 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Federal Insurance Office (Terrorism Risk Insurance Program)
regime: Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA); 31 CFR Part 50
title: Insurer must disclose terrorism premium and federal share on each commercial policy
requirement: As a condition of receiving federal payments, an insurer must give the policyholder clear and conspicuous disclosure of the premium charged for terrorism-insured losses and the federal share of compensation under the Program. The disclosure must appear as a separate line item and be made at the time of offer and at renewal.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR Part 50 disclosure subpart; in force as of 2026 as a condition of federal backstop payments.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Federal Insurance Office (Terrorism Risk Insurance Program)
regime: Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA); 31 CFR Part 50
title: Insurer must disclose the $100 billion Program cap to commercial policyholders
requirement: An insurer must provide clear and conspicuous disclosure to the policyholder of the existence of the $100,000,000,000 aggregate annual cap on federal and insurer liability under TRIA § 103(e)(2). This cap disclosure must be made at the time of offer, purchase, and renewal of each covered commercial policy.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR Part 50; separate cap disclosure required at offer, purchase, and renewal as of 2026.

regime: Price-Anderson Nuclear Industries Indemnity Act; 10 CFR Part 140
title: Nuclear reactor licensee must carry primary nuclear liability insurance
requirement: Each licensed power reactor of 100,000 electrical kW or greater must maintain the maximum available amount of primary nuclear liability insurance, increased by NRC rule from $450 million to $500 million effective January 1, 2024. Proof of the required financial protection is a condition of the operating license.
sourceNote: Verified via federalregister.gov NRC final rule; $500M primary layer effective Jan 1, 2024 and in force as of 2026.

regime: Price-Anderson Nuclear Industries Indemnity Act; 10 CFR Part 140
title: Reactor licensee must participate in secondary retrospective-premium layer
requirement: Each covered power reactor must maintain secondary financial protection through the industry retrospective rating pool, obligating the licensee to pay retrospective premiums (currently up to about $158 million per reactor, per incident) toward public compensation for a nuclear incident exceeding the primary insurance layer.
sourceNote: Verified via Congressional Research Service IF10821 and NRC nuclear insurance backgrounder; retrospective-premium secondary layer in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Medical Professional Liability Closed Claim Reporting Model Law (Model 77)
title: Medical professional liability insurer must file closed-claim reports
requirement: A medical professional liability insurer must report each closed claim to the state insurance department, including data on the claim, injury, indemnity and defense costs, and disposition, on the schedule and format prescribed by the adopting state. This supports state monitoring of the medical malpractice market.
citation: NAIC Model 77 (Medical Professional Liability Closed Claim Reporting); Guideline 1077
sourceNote: Verified on content.naic.org (Guideline 1077 implementing Model 77, adopted 2010); applies where a state has enacted closed-claim reporting, in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: USDA Risk Management Agency / Federal Crop Insurance Corporation
regime: Federal Crop Insurance Act; Standard Reinsurance Agreement (SRA)
title: Crop insurer must hold an approved SRA and remain financially eligible
requirement: An insurer writing federally reinsured multiple-peril crop insurance must execute and maintain a Standard Reinsurance Agreement with FCIC, and must be in good financial standing and in compliance with the laws of its state of domicile and the states where it writes, prior to and throughout approval as an Approved Insurance Provider.
sourceNote: Verified via rma.usda.gov 2026 SRA (dated 03-06-26); AIP eligibility and SRA execution in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: USDA Risk Management Agency / Federal Crop Insurance Corporation
regime: Federal Crop Insurance Act; RMA policy and procedure
title: Crop insurer must transmit acreage, production and policy data to RMA/FCIC
requirement: An Approved Insurance Provider must accept insured acreage reports by the applicable acreage reporting date and production reports by the production reporting date, and transmit policy, acreage, production and loss data to FCIC in the required electronic format (including through ACRSI where applicable) for reinsurance and program administration.
citation: 7 CFR Part 400 subpart P; SRA Appendix III data requirements
sourceNote: Verified via rma.usda.gov reinsurance-agreements and RMA procedure bulletins; AIP data-transmission duties in force as of 2026.

regime: Florida boiler safety / jurisdictional inspection law
title: Boiler and machinery insurer must perform jurisdictional inspections of insured objects
requirement: An insurer writing boiler and machinery (equipment breakdown) coverage in Florida must have insured boilers and pressure vessels inspected by special inspectors it employs and who are commissioned by the state; where an object is not insured, a state deputy inspector performs the jurisdictional inspection. Inspection results feed the state boiler certificate.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida DMS SPIP page describing insurer-employed special inspectors vs. deputy inspectors; boiler-inspection regime in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: North Carolina Office of State Fire Marshal
regime: North Carolina Uniform Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act
title: Boiler and machinery insurer inspectors must hold state commissions and report inspections
requirement: Special inspectors employed by an insurer authorized to write boiler and machinery insurance in North Carolina must be commissioned by the state, inspect insured boilers and pressure vessels at the intervals set by law, and file inspection reports with the Office of State Fire Marshal so that operating certificates can be issued.
citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 95 art. 7A (Uniform Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act)
sourceNote: Verified via ncosfm.gov boiler-and-machinery program page; commissioned insurer-inspector and reporting duties in force as of 2026.

regime: State boiler and machinery inspection statutes (multistate)
title: Boiler and machinery insurer may suspend coverage on a dangerously defective object
requirement: Upon an inspector finding an insured boiler or machinery object in a dangerous condition, the insurer may immediately suspend coverage on that specific object by delivering written notice to the insured. Coverage remains suspended until the hazard is repaired or removed; this is an absolute contractual and statutory right not requiring the insured's consent.
sourceNote: Verified as a standard state boiler-law/policy suspension right across jurisdictions; represents a distinct event-driven duty rather than a single citation.

regulatorName: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services
regime: State surety / bail bond producer licensing
title: Surety bail bond agents must be licensed insurance producers with surety authority
requirement: A person who executes or delivers a surety bail bond on behalf of an authorized surety and fidelity insurer must hold a resident insurance producer license with the surety (limited surety/bail bond) line of authority and be appointed by the insurer. Writing bail bonds without the license and appointment is prohibited.
citation: Mich. Comp. Laws (Insurance Code, producer licensing / bail bondsmen)
sourceNote: Verified via michigan.gov DIFS bail-bondsmen licensing page; producer license with surety authority required to write surety bail bonds as of 2026.

regime: Florida limited surety (bail bond) agent licensing
title: Limited surety (bail bond) agents must be licensed and appointed in Florida
requirement: An individual acting as a limited surety agent (bail bond agent) in Florida must obtain the 2-34 limited surety/bail bond agent license, meet education and examination requirements, and be appointed by an authorized surety insurer before soliciting, negotiating or executing bail bonds.
citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 648 (Bail Bond Agents); license type 2-34
sourceNote: Verified via myfloridacfo.com 2-34 limited surety/bail bond agent license document; in force as of 2026.

title: Idaho bail agents must file a $15,000 bond and maintain a surety appointment
requirement: A producer holding an Idaho bail license must file an original $15,000 bond with the Department and hold an appointment with a surety company; both the bond and the appointment must be continuously maintained or the bail license is deactivated.
sourceNote: Verified via doi.idaho.gov bail agent license page; $15,000 bond plus maintained appointment in force as of 2026.

title: Self-insured employer must qualify with the state before relying on excess WC cover
requirement: An employer seeking to self-insure workers' compensation in California must apply to and be approved by the Office of Self-Insurance Plans, meeting financial, security-deposit and program requirements; excess workers' compensation insurance covering losses above the self-insured retention is an optional layer that does not substitute for the state's qualification standards.
citation: Cal. Lab. Code § 3700 et seq.; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8 (OSIP)
sourceNote: Verified via dir.ca.gov OSIP self-insurance requirements; excess WC applies above the state-approved retention, in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC annual statement / large deductible & excess WC reporting
title: Insurer must report workers' compensation large-deductible and excess exposures in the annual statement
requirement: An insurer writing workers' compensation large-deductible or excess coverage for qualified self-insureds must report the associated premium, losses and recoverables in the NAIC financial annual statement blank consistent with NAIC large-deductible reporting guidance, so that regulators can evaluate net exposure and credit risk.
citation: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions (P&C); WC large-deductible reporting
sourceNote: Verified via content.naic.org WC large-deductible study and annual statement instructions; reporting treatment in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Property/Casualty Annual Statement (state page, medical malpractice)
title: Insurer must report medical malpractice premiums and losses on the annual statement state page
requirement: An insurer writing medical professional liability must report, by state, its written and earned premiums, paid and incurred losses, and expenses for the medical malpractice line on the state page of the NAIC P&C financial annual statement, giving each regulator statewide market data for that line.
citation: NAIC P&C Annual Statement Blank (state page; Schedule T Supplement A)
sourceNote: Verified via content.naic.org 2025 P&C annual statement blank; state-page medical malpractice reporting in force as of 2026.

title: Smaller reactor and non-power licensees must maintain formula-based nuclear liability protection
requirement: For reactors under 100 MWe and certain other licensees, the required primary financial protection is set by a formula based on reactor capacity and local population density, subject to a statutory floor of $4.5 million and ceiling of $74 million; the licensee must evidence this coverage as a license condition.
sourceNote: Verified via NRC nuclear insurance backgrounder and 10 CFR 140.12; $4.5M-$74M formula-based protection in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Congress / home-state insurance regulator (federal preemption framework)
title: Pay 100% of surplus-lines premium tax only to the insured's home state
requirement: Under the NRRA, no state other than the insured's home state may require any premium-tax payment for nonadmitted (surplus lines) insurance. The surplus-lines broker/insured must report and remit the applicable premium tax exclusively to the home state (principal place of business, or, for individuals, principal residence), which may allocate multistate tax by compact. Pass condition: full tax paid to the single home state.
sourceNote: Verified against 15 U.S.C. Ch. 108 subch. I text at uscode.house.gov; NRRA effective July 21, 2011, in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: Home-state insurance regulator (per NRRA federal framework)
title: Place and regulate nonadmitted insurance solely under the insured's home-state law
requirement: The placement of nonadmitted insurance is subject to the statutory and regulatory requirements solely of the insured's home state; no non-home state may require a surplus-lines broker to be licensed to sell, solicit, or negotiate that nonadmitted insurance. The broker must comply with home-state placement rules (broker licensing, diligent search, disclosures) and no other state's placement regime.
sourceNote: Verified 15 U.S.C. § 8202 at uscode.house.gov; home-state regulation rule in force since July 21, 2011.

regulatorName: Home-state insurance regulator (NRRA uniform eligibility standard)
title: Place surplus-lines business only with insurers meeting the $15M capital/surplus eligibility floor
requirement: Place surplus-lines business only with a US-domiciled insurer that maintains capital and surplus of at least $15M or the state minimum, whichever is greater (per NAIC model act)
sourceNote: Verified § 8204 at uscode.house.gov; $15M floor confirmed via Troutman surplusmanual.com and state DOI implementations (VT DFR); in force.

regulatorName: NAIC International Insurers Department (IID) / home-state regulator
regime: NRRA / NAIC IID Quarterly Listing of Alien Insurers
title: Place business with a non-US (alien) surplus-lines insurer only if on the NAIC IID Quarterly Listing
requirement: A surplus-lines broker may place nonadmitted business with an alien (non-U.S.-domiciled) insurer only if that insurer appears on the Quarterly Listing of Alien Insurers maintained by the NAIC International Insurers Department (IID). The broker must confirm current listing at each placement. Pass condition: insurer is on the then-current IID Quarterly Listing.
citation: 15 U.S.C. § 8204(b)(2); NAIC IID Quarterly Listing of Alien Insurers
sourceNote: Verified via NAIC surplus-lines topic page and Troutman surplusmanual.com; IID Quarterly Listing maintained and updated quarterly, current in 2026.

title: Skip the diligent-search requirement for qualifying exempt commercial purchasers
requirement: A surplus-lines broker placing coverage for an 'exempt commercial purchaser' need not perform the diligent-search of the admitted market, provided the broker discloses to the purchaser that the coverage may be available from an admitted insurer and the purchaser subsequently requests surplus-lines placement in writing. Pass condition: disclosure made and written request obtained before waiving diligent search.
sourceNote: Verified § 8205 at uscode.house.gov; exempt-commercial-purchaser exemption in force since 2011.

jurisdictionName: United States (NAIC Nonadmitted Insurance Model Act #870)
regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Model 870 as adopted)
title: Perform and document a diligent search of the admitted market before surplus-lines placement
requirement: Before placing coverage with an eligible surplus-lines insurer, the licensed surplus-lines broker must make a diligent search among admitted insurers actually writing that type of insurance in the state and document that the full amount or type could not be procured from admitted insurers. Most states require this to be evidenced by affidavit or a broker report filed with the placement.
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model 870 text (content.naic.org/model-law-870.pdf); 2023 revisions conform Model to NRRA; current model as of 2026.

jurisdictionName: United States (NAIC Nonadmitted Insurance Model Act #870)
regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Model 870 as adopted)
title: Deliver the surplus-lines nonadmitted-insurer disclosure notice to the insured
requirement: The surplus-lines licensee must deliver to the insured a written disclosure/notice that the insurance is placed with an insurer not licensed by the state and not protected by the state guaranty fund. The notice must be provided in the form and at the time required by the adopting state's version of Model 870. Pass condition: required disclosure delivered on/with the policy.
citation: NAIC Model 870 (Nonadmitted Insurance Model Act), disclosure provisions
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model 870 text; guaranty-fund/nonadmitted disclosure requirement current in 2026.

regulatorName: Surplus Lines Stamping Office of Texas (SLTX) / Texas Department of Insurance
regime: Texas Surplus Lines Stamping Office filing (SLTX)
title: File each Texas surplus-lines policy with SLTX within 60 days of effective/issue date
requirement: A Texas surplus-lines agent must file each surplus-lines insurance policy with the Surplus Lines Stamping Office of Texas (SLTX) no later than the 60th day after the later of the policy's effective date or issue date, and pay the associated stamping fee per SLTX's monthly invoice. Pass condition: policy submitted within 60 days and stamping fee timely paid.
citation: Tex. Ins. Code ch. 981; SLTX Compliance Guidelines (60-day filing)
sourceNote: Verified 60-day deadline and monthly stamping-fee invoicing on sltx.org compliance/billing pages; current 2026.

regulatorName: Florida Surplus Lines Service Office (FSLSO) / Florida Office of Insurance Regulation
regime: Florida Surplus Lines Service Office filing (FSLSO)
title: Electronically file each Florida premium-bearing surplus-lines transaction with FSLSO within 30 days
requirement: A Florida surplus-lines agent must electronically submit every premium-bearing surplus-lines policy transaction (taxable or non-taxable) to the FSLSO via SLIP+ (or prescribed XML/CSV batch format) within 30 days of the transaction's effective date, and remit the surplus-lines tax and FSLSO service fee. Pass condition: transaction filed within 30 days with tax/fee remitted.
citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 626 (Surplus Lines Law); FSLSO Filing Requirements (30-day)
sourceNote: Verified 30-day electronic-filing requirement directly on fslso.com filing-requirements page; current 2026.

regulatorName: Virginia Department of Taxation / Virginia Bureau of Insurance
regime: Virginia Surplus Lines Brokers Premium License Tax
title: File Virginia surplus-lines broker quarterly (Form 801) and annual reconciliation (Form 802) tax reports
requirement: A licensed Virginia surplus-lines broker must file quarterly surplus-lines premium license tax reports (Form 801) with tax remittance, and file an Annual Reconciliation Tax Report (Form 802) on or before March 1 for the prior year, if licensed for any part of the reporting period. Pass condition: quarterly returns and the March 1 annual reconciliation filed with tax paid.
citation: Va. Code § 58.1-2500 et seq.; VA Tax Forms 801/802
sourceNote: Verified Form 801 (quarterly) and Form 802 (annual reconciliation, due Mar 1) on tax.virginia.gov; 2026 forms published.

title: File Minnesota surplus-lines broker premium tax return (Form IG260) by Aug 15 and Feb 15
requirement: A licensed Minnesota surplus-lines broker must file Form IG260, Nonadmitted Insurance Premium Tax Return for Surplus Lines Brokers, semiannually by August 15 and February 15, and remit the nonadmitted-insurance premium tax on Minnesota home-state surplus-lines placements. Pass condition: both semiannual returns filed with tax paid.
citation: Minn. Stat. § 297I; MN DOR Form IG260
sourceNote: Verified Form IG260 semiannual Aug 15 / Feb 15 deadlines on revenue.state.mn.us; current 2026.

regulatorName: Vermont Department of Financial Regulation (Captive Insurance Division)
regime: Vermont Captive Insurance Companies (8 V.S.A. ch. 141)
title: File the Vermont Captive Insurance Company Annual Report verified by two executive officers
requirement: Every pure, association, sponsored, branch, or industrial-insured captive domiciled in Vermont must annually submit to the Commissioner a report of its financial condition (Vermont Captive Annual Report, VCAR), verified by the oath of two executive officers, in the prescribed form and electronically as a single PDF. Pass condition: annual report timely filed and verified.
sourceNote: Verified VCAR annual-report requirement and two-officer verification on dfr.vermont.gov filing-requirements; current 2026 (VCAR instructions rev. 12/2021).

regulatorName: Vermont Department of Taxes / Department of Financial Regulation
regime: Vermont Captive Insurance Premium Tax (8 V.S.A. § 6014)
title: Pay Vermont captive insurance premium tax on direct and assumed reinsurance premiums
requirement: A Vermont-licensed captive insurance company must annually compute and pay premium tax under 8 V.S.A. § 6014 on direct premiums written (net of returns) and on assumed reinsurance premiums for the prior calendar year, filing Form CPT-635. Pass condition: premium-tax return filed and tax paid by the statutory due date.
sourceNote: Verified § 6014 captive premium tax and Form CPT-635 on tax.vermont.gov; current 2026.

regulatorName: Delaware Department of Insurance (Bureau of Captive & Financial Insurance Products)
regime: Delaware Captive Insurance Companies (18 Del. C. ch. 69)
title: File Delaware captive annual report and pay captive premium tax by March 1 / April 15
requirement: A Delaware-licensed captive insurer must file an annual report of its financial condition under 18 Del. C. § 6907 and pay premium tax under § 6914 (0.2% of direct premiums up to $200k; 0.1% of assumed reinsurance up to $110k; $5,000 minimum) by April 15. Pass condition: annual report filed and premium tax remitted by the due date.
sourceNote: Verified § 6907 annual report and § 6914 premium-tax rates/April 15 due date via captive.delaware.gov and Delaware Code (delcode/justia); current 2026.

title: Submit an RRG plan of operation / feasibility study to the domiciliary commissioner before writing
requirement: Before offering insurance in any state, a risk retention group must submit to its domiciliary-state insurance commissioner a plan of operation or feasibility study covering the coverages, deductibles, coverage limits, rates, and rating classification systems for each line of commercial liability insurance it intends to write, and revisions thereto. Pass condition: plan/feasibility study filed and accepted before writing.
sourceNote: Verified § 3902(d)(1) plan-of-operation requirement at law.cornell.edu; LRRA in force (1986, amended).

title: Register the RRG and designate the commissioner as agent for process in each non-domiciliary state
requirement: To do business in a non-domiciliary state, a risk retention group must file the LRRA-specified registration (including its chartering documents, plan of operation, and financial statements) with that state and designate the state insurance commissioner as its agent solely for receiving service of legal process. Pass condition: registration and agent-designation on file in each state of operation.
sourceNote: Verified § 3902(d) non-domiciliary registration + agent-for-process at law.cornell.edu; in force.

regulatorName: Domiciliary state insurance regulator (NAIC accreditation standards)
regime: NAIC RRG financial-regulation standards (P&C annual statement)
title: File RRG P&C annual statement, audited financials, actuarial opinion, MD&A and RBC
requirement: A multistate risk retention group must comply with the same annual and quarterly P&C filing requirements as commercial insurers: the NAIC property/casualty Annual Statement blank, audited financial statements certified by an independent CPA, a statement of actuarial opinion on loss/LAE reserves by a qualified actuary, Management's Discussion & Analysis, and risk-based capital (RBC) reporting. Pass condition: full annual filing package submitted on time.
citation: NAIC Risk Retention & Purchasing Group Handbook; NAIC accreditation standards for RRGs
sourceNote: Verified RRG annual-statement/audit/actuarial-opinion/RBC filing set via NAIC RRG topic page and RRG FAQ (content.naic.org); current 2026.

regulatorName: Domiciliary state insurance regulator (NAIC RRG governance standards)
regime: NAIC RRG Corporate Governance Standards (accreditation, adopted 2011/2012)
