title: Maintain RRG board governance standards: independent directors, audit committee, service contracts
requirement: As a condition of NAIC accreditation, a risk retention group must satisfy corporate-governance standards including a majority-independent board elected by the owner/insureds, an independent audit committee, board-approved material service contracts on arm's-length terms, and written governance standards on director qualifications, orientation, and access to independent advisers. Pass condition: governance standards adopted and evidenced in filings/exams.
citation: NAIC RRG governance standards (2011/2012 accreditation revisions)
sourceNote: Verified RRG governance standards (independent board/audit committee/service-contract) via NAIC RRG topic page and captive.com/Faegre analyses; effective for accreditation since 2012.

regime: Liability Risk Retention Act — Purchasing Groups
title: File purchasing-group notice and designate commissioner as process agent in each state of operation
requirement: A risk purchasing group intending to do business in a state must furnish notice to that state's insurance commissioner specifying the lines and classifications of liability insurance it intends to purchase, its state of domicile and principal place of business, and the name/domicile of the insurer(s) from which coverage will be purchased, and must register and designate the commissioner as agent for service of process. Pass condition: notice/registration on file per state.
sourceNote: Verified § 3903 purchasing-group notice + agent-for-process at law.cornell.edu and uscode.house.gov; in force.

jurisdictionName: United States (NAIC Uniform Fraternal Code / Fraternal Benefit Society Model Act)
regulatorName: State insurance commissioners (via NAIC Model 675 as adopted)
regime: NAIC Uniform Fraternal Code / Fraternal Benefit Society Model Act (#675)
title: File the fraternal benefit society annual statement on the Life/Fraternal blank by March 1
requirement: A fraternal benefit society transacting insurance must annually file a financial-condition annual statement on the NAIC Life/Accident & Health/Fraternal Annual Statement blank with the domiciliary commissioner and NAIC, with all supplements and supporting schedules, by March 1. Pass condition: complete fraternal annual statement filed by the deadline.
citation: NAIC Model 675 (Uniform Fraternal Code); NAIC Fraternal Annual Statement Instructions
sourceNote: Fraternal regime confirmed as NAIC Model 675 (not 560) via content.naic.org model-law-675 and NAIC Life/Fraternal annual-statement instructions (Mar 1 due); current 2026. See coverageNotes on model-number discrepancy.

regime: California FAIR Plan — member-insurer assessment & recoupment (Bulletin 2024-8)
title: Pay FAIR Plan assessments as a member insurer; seek prior approval before recouping from policyholders
requirement: Every insurer licensed to write basic property lines in California is a FAIR Plan member and must pay its market-share proportional share of any FAIR Plan assessment. Per Bulletin 2024-8 (Sept 3, 2024), a member insurer that has paid an assessment may recoup it from policyholders only after filing a rule-change application and obtaining the Commissioner's prior approval. Pass condition: assessment paid; recoupment only via approved rule change.
sourceNote: Verified Bulletin 2024-8 (issued Sept 3, 2024) on insurance.ca.gov; assessment/recoupment framework current 2026.

regulatorName: DC Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking (DISB)
regime: DC Surplus Lines / Unauthorized Business Monthly Affidavit
title: File monthly affidavit of DC surplus-lines business placed by the 10th of the following month
requirement: A DC surplus-lines producer must file, under affidavit, a monthly report of all unauthorized (surplus-lines) business placed during the month, by the 10th day of the following month, per DC Code § 31-2502.40, and remit the associated premium tax. Pass condition: monthly affidavit report filed by the 10th with tax paid.
sourceNote: Verified monthly-affidavit-by-10th requirement referencing DC Code § 31-2502.40 via disb.dc.gov surplus-line information; current 2026.

regime: NAIC Variable Life Insurance Model Regulation (#270)
title: File and obtain approval of variable life policies, riders and variable-nature forms before issuance
requirement: Before delivery or issuance for delivery in a state, the insurer must file with and obtain the commissioner's approval of all variable life insurance policies plus every rider, endorsement, application and document relating to the variable nature of the policy. Mortality and expense risks must be borne by the insurer subject to the contract's stated maximums. Pass condition is prior written approval of every variable-nature form.
citation: NAIC Model Regulation #270 (Variable Life Insurance Model Regulation), Sec. 4
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #270 PDF and NAIC model-laws index; model current, adopted in most states as of 2026.

regime: Securities Act 1933 / Investment Company Act 1940 — Form N-6
title: Register variable life separate account and VUL policies with the SEC on Form N-6
requirement: An insurer offering variable life insurance (including variable universal life) must register the offering as a security under the Securities Act of 1933 and register the separate account as a unit investment trust under the Investment Company Act of 1940, using Form N-6. All new registration statements for such separate accounts filed on or after Dec 1, 2002 must use Form N-6. Pass condition is an effective N-6 registration statement.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 17 CFR 239.17c/274.11d and SEC 2002 adopting release; Form N-6 current as of 2026.

regime: SEC Rule 498A — Variable Contract Summary Prospectus
title: Deliver Rule 498A-compliant layered summary/statutory prospectus disclosure for VUL contracts
requirement: An insurer using a summary prospectus for a variable life (VUL) contract must comply with Rule 498A's layered-disclosure framework (initial and updating summary prospectuses, online access to the statutory prospectus/SAI). All initial registration statements and post-effective amendments on Form N-6 must comply with the amended disclosure requirements beginning Jan 1, 2022, and Inline XBRL tagging of certain disclosures is required from Jan 1, 2023.
sourceNote: Verified against SEC Press Release 2020-57; compliance dates Jan 1 2022 (N-6) and Jan 1 2023 (Inline XBRL), current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation (#582)
title: Submit signed basic illustration or no-illustration acknowledgment at application
requirement: For life policies with illustrated death benefits over $10,000 (variable life, credit life and annuities excepted), if an illustration is used and the policy is applied for as illustrated, the producer must submit to the insurer a basic illustration signed by producer and applicant at time of application; if no illustration is used, both must sign an insurer-provided acknowledgment that none was used. Pass condition is the correct signed record on file.
citation: NAIC Model Regulation #582 (Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation), Sec. 6
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #582 PDF and NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations topic page; model current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation (#582)
title: Appoint an illustration actuary and file annual illustration-scale certification
requirement: Each insurer that markets illustrated life policies must have its board appoint at least one qualified illustration actuary who annually certifies that the disciplined current scale conforms to ASOP No. 24 (Compliance with NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation) and that illustrated scales meet the regulation. The certification and required disclosures must be provided to the state regulator. Pass condition is a timely, conforming annual certification on file.
citation: NAIC Model Regulation #582, Sec. 11 (Annual Certifications); ASOP No. 24
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #582 PDF and Actuarial Standards Board ASOP No. 24; requirement current as of 2026.

title: Illustrate indexed universal life per AG 49-A benchmark-index and multiplier constraints
requirement: For indexed universal life policies with index-linked credits sold on or after Dec 14, 2020, illustrations must comply with AG 49-A: cap the maximum illustrated annual rate of index credits to a single benchmark index account, prevent charge-based/multiplier features from illustrating a net benefit greater than a non-enhanced product, and limit illustrated loan leverage to no more than 50 basis points. Pass condition is IUL illustrations conforming to AG 49-A.
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC AG XLIX-A document; effective for policies sold on/after Dec 14, 2020, current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Standard Nonforfeiture Law for Life Insurance (#808)
title: Include minimum guaranteed nonforfeiture and cash-surrender-value provisions in life policies
requirement: Every life insurance policy issued on/after the operative date must contain nonforfeiture provisions at least as favorable to the policyholder as the statutory minimums: a cash surrender value on default after 3 full years (ordinary) or 5 (industrial) of premiums paid, an automatic paid-up nonforfeiture benefit unless another option is elected within 60 days, and a statement of the mortality table and interest rate used. Pass condition is policy provisions meeting or exceeding the minimums.
citation: NAIC Model #808 (Standard Nonforfeiture Law for Life Insurance), Secs. 3-5
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #808 PDF; last amended 2014, current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Universal Life Insurance Model Regulation (#585)
title: Guarantee minimum cash surrender values and provide annual report on universal life policies
requirement: For universal life insurance policies, any surrender charge must leave a net value not less than the minimum cash surrender value computed under the regulation, and the insurer must furnish the policyowner a periodic (at least annual) report of policy value, cash surrender value, death benefit, premiums paid and charges deducted. Where cash value rests on multiple guaranteed rate/charge/mortality sets, each set must independently satisfy nonforfeiture. Pass condition is compliant minimum values and timely annual reporting.
citation: NAIC Model #585 (Universal Life Insurance Model Regulation), Secs. 5 & 8
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #585 PDF (minimum cash surrender value and annual report provisions); current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Life Insurance and Annuities Replacement Model Regulation (#613)
title: Follow replacement-transaction duties: notice, existing-insurer notification and record retention
requirement: In a life insurance replacement or financed-purchase transaction, the producer must obtain a signed statement whether replacement is involved, present and leave a Notice Regarding Replacement, and the replacing insurer must notify each existing insurer within required timeframes and retain replacement records. On request, the existing insurer must furnish an in-force illustration or policy summary. Pass condition is completed replacement documentation and timely existing-insurer notification.
citation: NAIC Model #613 (Life Insurance and Annuities Replacement Model Regulation), Secs. 5-6
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #613 PDF (2015 edition); current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation (#570)
title: Ensure life insurance advertisements are truthful, non-misleading and maintain an advertising file
requirement: All life insurance advertisements (print, digital, broadcast, social media) must give full and truthful disclosure, avoid untrue or misleading claims and unfair comparisons/disparagement, be understandable to an average consumer, and be substantiated. The insurer must maintain a complete advertising file of all advertisements with a notation of manner and extent of distribution for the required retention period. Pass condition is compliant advertisements and a current advertising file.
citation: NAIC Model #570 (Advertisements of Life Insurance and Annuities Model Regulation), Secs. 4-16
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #570 PDF; last revised 2015, current as of 2026.

title: Provide accelerated-benefit tax disclosure and obtain assignee/beneficiary acknowledgment before payout
requirement: For accelerated benefit provisions of individual and group life policies, the insurer must give a disclosure statement (at application/issue and at benefit request) that the accelerated benefit may be taxable and a tax advisor should be consulted, offer a lump-sum settlement option, place no restrictions on use of proceeds, and obtain a signed concurrence from any assignee or irrevocable beneficiary before paying. Reserves must follow the Standard Valuation Law. Pass condition is the required disclosures, acknowledgment and reserving.
citation: NAIC Model #620 (Accelerated Benefits Model Regulation), Secs. 7-9
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #620 PDF; current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Group Life Insurance Standard Provisions Model Act (#565)
title: Issue individual certificates to each insured under a group life policy
requirement: A group life insurance policy must contain a provision requiring the insurer to issue to the policyholder, for delivery to each insured person, a certificate setting forth the insurance protection to which the insured is entitled, to whom benefits are payable, any dependent coverage, and the conversion and other rights. For debtor group life, a certificate describing the coverage and death-benefit application must be furnished to each insured debtor. Pass condition is delivery of conforming certificates to all insureds.
citation: NAIC Model #565 (Group Life Insurance Definition and Standard Provisions Model Act), Sec. 5
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #565 PDF (certificate delivery / standard provisions); current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Group Life Insurance Standard Provisions Model Act (#565)
title: Include a conversion privilege on termination of group life coverage
requirement: A group life policy must contain a provision granting each insured whose coverage terminates (by termination of eligibility or of the group policy) the right to convert, without evidence of insurability and within the stated conversion period, to an individual life policy on a permitted plan up to the amount of terminated group insurance. Pass condition is a conversion-privilege provision meeting the model's minimum terms.
citation: NAIC Model #565, Sec. 5 (Standard Provisions — Conversion Privilege)
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #565 PDF (standard provisions include conversion on termination); current as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Term and Universal Life Insurance Reserve Financing Model Regulation (#787)
title: Hold Primary/Other Security for XXX/AXXX captive reserve-financing arrangements
requirement: For reserve-financing (captive reinsurance) arrangements on term life (Reg XXX) and universal life with secondary guarantees (Reg AXXX), the ceding insurer must ensure Primary Security and Other Security are held by or on behalf of the cedant in the required forms and amounts, with the Reserve Actuarial Method applied treaty-by-treaty per VM-20; the appointed actuary must analyze the adequacy of assets. Pass condition is holding the required security or the arrangement triggers regulatory consequences.
citation: NAIC Model #787 (Term and Universal Life Insurance Reserve Financing Model Regulation), Secs. 4-6
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #787 PDF and NAIC government-affairs brief; an NAIC accreditation standard, current as of 2026.

title: Register variable annuity separate account offerings on Form N-4 with summary prospectus
requirement: An insurer offering individual variable annuity contracts through a separate account (unit investment trust) must register the offering on SEC Form N-4 under the Securities Act of 1933 and keep the registration statement effective and current. Under Rule 498A the issuer may satisfy statutory prospectus delivery by giving investors an initial summary prospectus and posting the full statutory prospectus online. Pass = effective N-4 registration and compliant layered disclosure delivery.
sourceNote: Verified on eCFR/Cornell LII and SEC Form N-4; Rule 498A summary-prospectus framework adopted 2020 (Rel. 33-10765), in force July 2026.

title: Register RILA and registered MVA annuity offerings on amended Form N-4
requirement: An issuer of a registered index-linked annuity (RILA) or a registered market-value-adjustment (MVA) annuity must register the offering on the amended Form N-4 (the new tailored form for these products) rather than S-1/S-3, providing the tailored key-information, fee, and risk disclosures. Mandatory compliance began May 1, 2026. Pass = RILA/MVA offering registered and disclosed on the amended N-4.
sourceNote: Verified Federal Register + SEC final rule PDF (33-11294); effective Sept 23, 2024, compliance date May 1, 2026 (in force July 2026).

regime: Securities Act Rule 156 (extended to non-variable annuities)
title: Ensure RILA/MVA sales literature is not materially misleading under Rule 156
requirement: The SEC extended Rule 156 to advertisements and sales literature for non-variable (RILA and registered MVA) annuities, so issuers must ensure such materials are not materially misleading, including balanced presentation of fees, index-crediting limits (caps/participation rates), interim value and market-value adjustments, and withdrawal/surrender charges. Pass = sales literature reviewed against Rule 156 factors.
sourceNote: Verified SEC press release 2024-81 and final rule; Rule 156 extension effective with RILA rule (in force 2026).

title: Principal review and suitability determination before submitting deferred variable annuity applications
requirement: A FINRA member recommending a purchase or exchange of a deferred variable annuity must have a registered principal review and approve/reject the transaction, documented and signed, no later than seven business days after the OSJ receives a complete application, and only if there is a reasonable basis to believe the transaction is suitable. Members must also maintain supervisory procedures and product-specific training. Pass = documented principal review within the deadline.
sourceNote: Verified on FINRA rulebook; Rule 2330 in force July 2026.

title: Deliver annuity disclosure document and Buyer's Guide at or before application
requirement: For fixed, fixed-indexed and variable annuities, the insurer/producer must, in a face-to-face sale, give the applicant both the disclosure document and the Buyer's Guide at or before application; in non-face-to-face sales, both must be sent. The disclosure document must describe contract features, charges, and the like. Pass = documented delivery of both items to the applicant.
citation: NAIC Model #245, Sec. 5-6 (Annuity Disclosure Model Regulation)
sourceNote: Verified NAIC Model #245 PDF; buyer's-guide separation confirmed; adopted by most states, in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Annuity Disclosure Model Regulation (#245) - illustrations
title: Provide annuity illustrations conforming to Model 245 standards on request/use
requirement: Where an insurer provides an annuity illustration, it must conform to the illustration standards in Model #245, including that illustrated figures be based on defined interest/index-crediting assumptions and be accompanied by required disclosures so as not to mislead. Pass = illustrations comply with the model's illustration section.
citation: NAIC Model #245 (Annuity Disclosure Model Regulation), illustration provisions
sourceNote: Verified NAIC Model #245; illustration standards distinct from AG 49-A. In force 2026.

title: Cap indexed annuity/IUL illustrated crediting rates under AG 49-A disciplined current scale
requirement: For index-linked products, the illustrated annual rate of indexed credits must not exceed the AG 49-A disciplined-current-scale maximum (benchmark index account earned-interest limit) and illustrations must not present supplemental/historical index figures that exceed the maximum illustrated rate. Amendments standardizing historical periods and limiting side-by-side comparisons take effect April 1, 2026. Pass = illustrated rates within the AG 49-A ceiling.
sourceNote: Verified NAIC AG 49-A drafts; Sec. 7.B/7.C amendments effective April 1, 2026 (adopted by LATF Nov 13, 2025; A Cmte Nov 21, 2025).

title: Hold principle-based reserves for variable annuities under VM-21 (stochastic + standard amount)
requirement: An insurer writing variable annuities within the scope of VM-21 must hold the greater of a stochastic reserve (CTE-based) plus an additional standard amount, computed per the principle-based Variable Annuity Framework. Reserves are set at least annually as part of statutory valuation. Pass = VM-21-compliant reserves supported by the required actuarial modeling.
sourceNote: Verified current Valuation Manual (Jan 1 2026 edition); VM-21 effective since 1/1/2020, current 2026.

title: Apply AG 43 CARVM reserving to variable annuities issued before the Valuation Manual
requirement: For variable annuity contracts issued on/after Jan 1, 1981 and prior to Valuation Manual adoption, the insurer must reserve under Actuarial Guideline XLIII (CARVM for variable annuities), which references the VM-21 methodology, to determine minimum statutory reserves. Pass = AG 43-compliant reserves for in-scope legacy contracts.
sourceNote: Verified via NAIC/Academy VM-21 materials and IRS LB&I directive referencing AG 43/VM-21; in force 2026.

title: File VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report documenting variable annuity principle-based reserves
requirement: An insurer computing variable annuity reserves under VM-21 must prepare and provide, on regulator request, a VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report documenting assumptions, methods, models, margins and results supporting the principle-based valuation. Pass = complete VM-31 report available/filed for the valuation date.
sourceNote: Verified current Valuation Manual; VM-31 documents VM-21 PBR work; in force 2026.

regime: Standard Nonforfeiture Law for Individual Deferred Annuities (#805)
title: Provide minimum nonforfeiture values on individual deferred annuities under Model 805
requirement: An insurer issuing individual deferred non-variable (fixed / fixed-indexed) annuities must guarantee minimum nonforfeiture amounts of at least 87.5% of gross premiums accumulated at the nonforfeiture interest rate (5-year CMT less 125 bps, floor 0.15%, cap 3%), less specified deductions. Pass = contract nonforfeiture values meet or exceed the Model 805 minimum.
citation: NAIC Model #805, Standard Nonforfeiture Law for Individual Deferred Annuities
sourceNote: Verified NAIC Model #805 PDF; 87.5%/CMT-125bp mechanics confirmed; state-adopted, in force 2026.

title: Apply annuity solvency and consumer-protection rules to contingent deferred annuities
requirement: An insurer writing contingent deferred annuities (guaranteeing lifetime payments once contractually-defined external assets are depleted) must be a licensed life insurer and apply the NAIC-identified set of annuity solvency and consumer-protection laws to CDAs; the Buyer's Guide requirement is expressly excluded until an NAIC CDA-specific guide exists, and producers must hold securities/variable licensing. Pass = CDA program written by a life insurer under the identified regime.
citation: NAIC CDA Working Group guidance (Life Insurance and Annuities (A) Committee)
sourceNote: Verified NAIC A Committee CDA guidelines document; guidance framework, adopted by states variably, current 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration
title: Select 'safest available annuity' when transferring pension liabilities to a group annuity
requirement: In a pension risk transfer, the plan fiduciary purchasing group annuities to discharge defined-benefit obligations must conduct an objective, thorough, and analytical search and take steps to obtain the safest annuity available, assessing the six IB 95-1 provider factors (portfolio quality/diversification, capital, guaranty-association coverage, etc.), unless it is in participants' interest to do otherwise. Pass = documented safest-available-annuity selection process.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR/Cornell LII; DOL confirmed IB 95-1 unchanged after SECURE 2.0 Sec. 321 review; in force 2026.

title: File Form 1098-Q and furnish participant statement for qualified longevity annuity contracts
requirement: An insurer issuing a contract intended to be a qualifying longevity annuity contract (QLAC) must file Form 1098-Q with the IRS and furnish the participant statement annually, beginning the first premium year and continuing until the year before the participant dies or reaches age 85, reporting premiums, FMV, and annuity start/amount. IRS deadlines: recipient copy by Jan 31; IRS by Feb 28 (paper) / Mar 31 (e-file). Pass = timely, accurate 1098-Q filing and statements.
sourceNote: Verified IRS Form 1098-Q instructions (Rev. Apr 2025); QLAC $210,000 limit and reporting cadence current 2026.

regime: Final RMD Regulations (SECURE / SECURE 2.0), Treas. Reg. 1.401(a)(9)
title: Apply RMD annuity-aggregation and partial-annuitization rules under 2024 final regulations
requirement: For qualified annuities, plans and IRAs may (and issuers must administer so as to permit) aggregating the annuity's fair market value with the remaining account balance for RMD calculation, counting annuity payments toward the total RMD; partial annuitization is valued using the gift-tax method beginning with the 2026 distribution year. Pass = annuity RMD administration conforms to the final 401(a)(9) regulations effective Sept 17, 2024.
sourceNote: Verified IRS/Treasury final RMD regs published July 19, 2024, effective Sept 17, 2024; gift-tax-method valuation for 2026 distribution year.

title: Provide a free-look cancellation period on annuity contracts (minimum ~10-30 days by state)
requirement: Insurers must include a free-look (right-to-examine) provision allowing the contract owner to return the annuity within the state-mandated period (commonly 10-30 days, with longer windows for senior buyers) beginning on contract delivery, for a full refund of premium without surrender charge. Pass = compliant free-look language and honored cancellations.
citation: State insurance codes (annuity free-look provisions); NAIC-referenced
sourceNote: Verified via NAIC annuities topic and state summaries; free-look is a state statutory requirement (day count varies), in force 2026. Not a single NAIC model number.

regime: RILA Rule / interim-value & withdrawal-charge disclosure (Form N-4)
title: Disclose RILA surrender charges, interim value adjustments, and market-value adjustments on Form N-4
requirement: A RILA/MVA issuer using Form N-4 must clearly disclose the three withdrawal-related charge mechanisms - surrender charges, interim value adjustments (IVAs) applied to index-linked options withdrawn before crediting-period end, and positive/negative market-value adjustments - along with index caps/participation rates, so investors understand contract-value impacts of early withdrawal. Pass = N-4 discloses all applicable adjustments.
sourceNote: Verified SEC final rule 33-11294; IVA/MVA/surrender disclosure requirements on amended N-4, compliance May 1, 2026.

title: File annual Medicare Supplement loss-ratio refund calculation by May 31
requirement: A Medicare Supplement (Medigap) issuer must file, for each state and policy form, an annual refund calculation form comparing cumulative actual incurred loss ratios to the minimum benchmark (65% individual, 75% group) and refund/credit any deficiency. It is filed for the prior calendar year and due by May 31 of the following year.
citation: NAIC Model #651 (Medicare Supplement Insurance Minimum Standards), Loss Ratio Standards & Refund/Credit provisions (Appendix A refund form)
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #651 PDF; loss-ratio refund form due May 31 (e.g., CY2025 due 5/31/2026); in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

title: Honor six-month Medigap open-enrollment guaranteed issue without underwriting
requirement: A Medicare Supplement issuer must, during an applicant's six-month Medigap open-enrollment period (beginning the first month the person is 65+ and enrolled in Part B) and in defined guaranteed-issue situations, issue any offered Medigap policy without medical underwriting and without pre-existing-condition rating or denial.
citation: NAIC Model #651, Guaranteed Issue for Eligible Persons / Open Enrollment provisions (implementing 42 U.S.C. 1395ss)
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #651 and Medicare.gov; federal 6-month open-enrollment guaranteed issue in force as of 2026.

regime: Medicare Advantage / Part D bidding (Part C & D)
title: Submit annual Medicare Advantage/Part D bids by the first Monday in June
requirement: A Medicare Advantage organization and Part D sponsor must submit annual plan bids (benefit and pricing packages) to CMS for the upcoming contract year by the statutory deadline of the first Monday in June (June 1, 2026 for CY2027). CMS reviews and negotiates bids before approval.
citation: Social Security Act §1854 / §1860D-11; 42 CFR 422 Subpart F and 42 CFR 423 Subpart F
sourceNote: Verified against CMS bidding instructions/fact sheets; first-Monday-in-June deadline (6/1/2026 for CY2027) in force as of 2026.

regime: Medicare Advantage/Part D Minimum MLR (Part 422/423 Subpart X)
title: File annual Medicare Advantage/Part D MLR report and meet 85% minimum
requirement: A Medicare Advantage organization and Part D sponsor must annually report its medical loss ratio for each contract to CMS in HPMS and maintain an MLR of at least 85 percent; failure triggers remittance, and sustained failure can trigger enrollment sanctions or contract termination. Records must be retained 10 years.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR Part 422 Subpart X and CMS MLR filing instructions (CY2024 report due Dec 2025); 85% minimum in force as of 2026.

title: Deliver annual ANOC by Sept 30 and Evidence of Coverage by Oct 15
requirement: A Medicare Advantage organization must provide each current enrollee the standardized Annual Notice of Change (ANOC) for receipt by September 30 and the Evidence of Coverage (EOC) by October 15 each year, disclosing service area, benefits, cost-sharing, access, and grievance/appeal procedures for the upcoming plan year.
citation: 42 CFR 422.111 and 42 CFR 422.2267 (ANOC/EOC required materials and delivery deadlines)
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 422.111 and 422.2267; ANOC by Sept 30, EOC by Oct 15 in force as of 2026.

regime: Medicare Advantage/Part D marketing review (Part 422 Subpart V)
title: Submit MA/Part D marketing materials to CMS via HPMS before use
requirement: A Medicare Advantage organization must submit marketing materials, election forms, and certain designated communications materials to CMS through the HPMS Marketing Module for review before distribution; materials may be used only after CMS disposition, deemed approval (45 days, or 10 days for model materials), or the applicable 5-day file-and-use window.
citation: 42 CFR 422.2261 (Submission, review, and distribution of materials)
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 422.2261; HPMS pre-distribution submission/deemed-approval windows in force as of 2026.

regime: Medicare Advantage Risk Adjustment Data (RADV, Part 422 Subpart G)
title: Submit medical records for RADV audits and remit improper risk-adjustment payments
requirement: A Medicare Advantage organization must ensure the accuracy of submitted risk-adjustment (diagnosis) data, submit sampled medical records for CMS Risk Adjustment Data Validation audits, and remit improper payments identified by RADV; under the 2023 final rule CMS may extrapolate contract-level audit findings for payment years 2018 forward.
citation: 42 CFR 422.310 (Risk adjustment data); RADV Final Rule 88 FR 6643 (Feb 1, 2023)
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 422.310 and 2023 RADV final rule; note Humana v. Becerra (Sept 2025) vacated the rule on APA procedural grounds, so extrapolation methodology is in litigation-driven flux as of 2026.

title: Submit annual Medicaid MCO medical loss ratio report to the state
requirement: A Medicaid managed care organization (MCO/PIHP/PAHP) must calculate and report a medical loss ratio to the contracting state for each MLR reporting year consistent with 42 CFR 438.8; where a state sets a minimum MLR it must be at least 85% with remittance, and the state submits summary MLR reports to CMS through MDCT-MCR with its annual rate certification.
citation: 42 CFR 438.8 and 42 CFR 438.74 (MLR standards; state MLR summary reporting)
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 438.8/438.74 and Medicaid.gov MLR guidance; MDCT-MCR submission required for rating periods on/after 7/1/2024; in force as of 2026.

title: Collect and submit accurate, complete Medicaid enrollee encounter data
requirement: A Medicaid MCO/PIHP/PAHP must maintain systems to collect enrollee encounter data, verify its accuracy, timeliness, completeness and consistency, submit it to the state in CMS/state-specified standardized formats and frequency, and make it available to the state and, on request, to CMS.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 438.242; encounter data collection/verification/submission obligations in force as of 2026.

title: Provide Medicaid enrollee handbook, provider directory, and required disclosures
requirement: A Medicaid MCO/PIHP/PAHP must furnish enrollees an enrollee handbook and an accurate, accessible provider directory (per 438.10(h)) in an easily understood, readily accessible manner; the state contracts an independent entity to run annual secret-shopper surveys verifying provider-directory compliance.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR 438.10; enrollee handbook, provider directory and annual secret-shopper survey requirements in force as of 2026.

regime: Federal Employees Health Benefits Program (5 CFR Part 890)
title: Submit annual FEHB benefit and rate proposal by May 31 via Carrier Connect
requirement: An FEHB-participating carrier must submit its annual benefit and rate proposal to OPM (through Carrier Connect) no later than May 31 for the following plan year, following its documented community-rating or experience-rating methodology; community-rated carriers (other than TCR) must meet the FEHB-specific MLR threshold published in OPM's annual rate instructions.
citation: 5 U.S.C. 8902; 5 CFR Part 890; OPM FEHB Program Carrier Letters (annual rate instructions)
sourceNote: Verified against 5 CFR 890 and OPM 2025/2026 FEHB carrier letters; May 31 rate-proposal deadline and FEHB-specific MLR in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Long-Term Care Insurance Model Regulation (Model 641) rate stability
title: File LTC rate-increase actuarial certification and 3-year updated projections
requirement: A long-term care insurer, when implementing a premium rate increase on rate-stability policies, must file for the commissioner's review updated projections annually for the next three years with a comparison of actual to projected results, supported by an actuarial memorandum signed by a member of the American Academy of Actuaries complying with ASOP No. 18.
citation: NAIC Model #641, Section 20 (Premium Rate Schedule Increases) / Section 9 (initial rate certification)
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #641 PDF; rate-stability certification and 3-year projection filing in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Long-Term Care Insurance Model Act (Model 640)
title: Offer LTC inflation protection and obtain signed rejection if declined
requirement: A long-term care insurer must offer each applicant, at the time of purchase, a policy with a meaningful inflation-protection benefit no less favorable than the model's defined options; inflation protection must be included in the policy unless the insurer obtains a rejection signed by the policyholder.
citation: NAIC Model #640, Section 6F (Inflation Protection) and related nonforfeiture/suitability provisions
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #640 PDF; inflation-protection offer/signed-rejection requirement in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

title: Obtain HMO certificate of authority and file evidence-of-coverage forms and rates
requirement: A health maintenance organization must obtain and maintain a certificate of authority from the commissioner and file its evidence-of-coverage forms and premium rates (for prior approval or file-and-use per state option), and satisfy net-worth and deposit requirements, to lawfully operate as an HMO.
citation: NAIC Model #430 (HMO Model Act), certificate of authority, form/rate filing, and net-worth/deposit provisions
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #430 PDF; HMO certificate of authority + form/rate filing + net-worth/deposit in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Health Benefit Plan Network Access and Adequacy Model Act (Model 74)
title: File and maintain a network access plan demonstrating network adequacy
requirement: A health carrier offering a network plan must create and file with the commissioner (for approval or review per state option) an access plan demonstrating adequate, accessible provider networks, and maintain networks meeting the model's adequacy standards including protections against balance/surprise billing.
citation: NAIC Model #74 (Health Benefit Plan Network Access and Adequacy Model Act), access plan provisions
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #74 PDF (2015 revisions); access-plan filing and network adequacy standards in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Utilization Review and Benefit Determination Model Act (Model 73)
title: Operate a compliant utilization review program with timely benefit determinations
requirement: A health carrier (or its utilization-review designee) must maintain a utilization review and benefit determination program meeting the model's structure, clinical-review-criteria, personnel, and timeframe standards for prospective, concurrent, and retrospective determinations, and treat any adverse determination as appealable under the grievance model act.
citation: NAIC Model #73 (Utilization Review and Benefit Determination Model Act)
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #73 PDF; UR program/timeframe standards aligned with ACA internal-appeals rules, in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Uniform Health Carrier External Review Model Act (Model 75)
title: Provide independent external review of adverse benefit determinations and pay IRO cost
requirement: A health carrier must give covered persons access to external review of adverse and final adverse benefit determinations by a commissioner-assigned approved Independent Review Organization, comply with standard and expedited timeframes (expedited decision within 72 hours), and pay the cost of the IRO conducting the review.
citation: NAIC Model #75 (Uniform Health Carrier External Review Model Act), IRO assignment/timeframe/cost provisions
sourceNote: Verified against NAIC Model #75 PDF and 45 CFR 147.136 alignment; external-review/IRO obligations in force via state adoptions as of 2026.

title: Submit annual RxDC prescription drug and health-care spending report by June 1
requirement: A group health plan and health insurance issuer (including the fully-insured and self-insured plans it administers) must submit the annual RxDC report to CMS by June 1 for the prior reference year, including plan-level premium/enrollment (D1/P2) data and information on the most-dispensed, costliest, and highest-rebate drugs and total health-care spending.
citation: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021, §204; 26 CFR 54.9825-4T / 29 CFR 2590.725-4 / 45 CFR 149.740 (PHS Act §2799A-10)
sourceNote: Verified against CMS RxDC page; 2025 reference-year report due June 1, 2026; distinct from MLR/parity/APCD; in force as of 2026.

title: No kickbacks or unearned fees for referral of title/settlement services
requirement: The title insurance underwriter and its agents must not give or accept any fee, kickback, or thing of value pursuant to any agreement that settlement-service business (including title insurance) incident to a federally related mortgage loan will be referred to any person. Compliance is judged transaction-by-transaction; violations carry treble-damage and criminal exposure. Pass condition: no compensated referrals and any payment reflects goods/services actually rendered at market value.
sourceNote: Verified on consumerfinance.gov (Reg X §1024.14) and uscode.house.gov (12 USC 2607); in force as of 2026.

title: No fee-splitting for title/settlement services not actually performed
requirement: The insurer and its title agents must not give or accept any portion, split, or percentage of a charge for a settlement service (e.g., title premium) in a federally related mortgage transaction other than for services actually performed. Marking up a third party's charge with no additional service is prohibited. Pass condition: every split corresponds to a bona fide service rendered.
sourceNote: Verified on law.cornell.edu (12 USC 2607) and Reg X §1024.14; in force as of 2026.

regime: RESPA / Regulation X Affiliated Business Arrangements
title: Provide Affiliated Business Arrangement Disclosure when referring to affiliated title agent
requirement: When the insurer or its loan officer refers a consumer to an affiliated title insurance agency in a federally related mortgage transaction, it must give a written Affiliated Business Arrangement Disclosure (Appendix D format) at or before referral, describing the ownership/financial interest and estimated charges, must not require use of the affiliate, and must retain the disclosure for 5 years. Pass condition: timely disclosure, no required use, records kept.
sourceNote: Verified on consumerfinance.gov and ecfr.gov (12 CFR 1024.15); in force as of 2026.

regulatorName: Federal Housing Finance Agency (Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac)
title: Maintain Available Assets at or above Minimum Required Assets under PMIERs
requirement: To remain an approved insurer for GSE-acquired loans, a private mortgage guaranty insurer must maintain 'Available Assets' (most-liquid assets) equal to or exceeding its risk-based 'Minimum Required Assets' computed from its insurance-in-force. The 2024 update tightens the Available Asset definition by credit quality/liquidity, phased in through a fully-effective date of Sept. 30, 2026. Pass condition: Available Assets >= Minimum Required Assets each reporting period.
sourceNote: Verified on fhfa.gov 2024 news release and Freddie Mac PMIERs page; fully effective 2026-09-30.

regulatorName: Federal Housing Finance Agency (Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac)
regime: GSE Rescission Relief Principles (PMIERs Exhibit G)
title: Structure MI master policy rescission-relief provisions per GSE Principles
requirement: An approved private mortgage insurer must structure the incontestability/rescission-relief provisions of its GSE master policy to conform to the Amended and Restated GSE Rescission Relief Principles, aligning rescission rights with the GSE Representation & Warranty Framework so that only Significant Defects permit rescission and other defects are subject only to repricing. Pass condition: master policy on file conforms to Exhibit G Principles.
citation: PMIERs Exhibit G — GSE Rescission Relief Principles (amended)
sourceNote: Verified on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac PMIERs Exhibit G documents; in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (#630)
title: Establish and maintain a mortgage-guaranty contingency reserve (50% of net premium)
requirement: A mortgage guaranty insurer must establish a contingency reserve out of net premium remaining after the unearned premium reserve, contributing an amount equal to 50% of that net earned premium, and maintain each year's contribution for 120 months. Withdrawals are allowed only in years where incurred losses exceed 35% of earned premiums, and releases require domiciliary-commissioner approval. Pass condition: reserve funded, held, and released only as permitted.
citation: NAIC Model #630, Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act, § on contingency reserve
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #630 PDF on content.naic.org (rev. May 2023); adopted variously by states, in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (#630)
title: Keep mortgage-guaranty risk-in-force within 25:1 of capital, surplus and contingency reserve
requirement: A mortgage guaranty insurer must not carry total outstanding risk in force exceeding 25 times the sum of its capital, surplus, and contingency reserve (the '25-to-1' limit). Exceeding the ratio requires the insurer to cease writing new business until the ratio is restored. Pass condition: aggregate net risk-in-force <= 25 x (capital + surplus + contingency reserve).
citation: NAIC Model #630, Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Model Act (risk-to-capital limit)
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #630 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act (#360)
title: Refund unearned credit-insurance premium on early termination within 30 days
requirement: Refund unearned credit-insurance premium on early termination (make appropriate refund or credit of the unearned charge)
citation: NAIC Model #360, Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act, § on refunds
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #360 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model Regulation (#370)
title: Demonstrate a 60% minimum loss ratio for credit-insurance rate deviations
requirement: An insurer using rates above the prima facie schedule (a deviation under Model #370) for credit life or credit A&H must file supporting experience showing the rate develops, or may reasonably be expected to develop, a loss ratio of not less than 60% across its total consumer credit insurance business (including affiliates) for each coverage type. Pass condition: filed rates meet the 60% loss-ratio benchmark.
citation: NAIC Model #370, Consumer Credit Insurance Model Regulation, § 9-11 (deviations / loss ratio)
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #370 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.

regime: Truth in Lending Act / Regulation Z
title: Provide credit-insurance disclosures and obtain affirmative written consent to exclude premium from finance charge
requirement: For voluntary credit insurance (life, A&H, unemployment) or debt-cancellation/suspension coverage sold with credit, the creditor must disclose that the coverage is optional, disclose the premium/fee, and obtain the consumer's signed or initialed affirmative written request after the disclosures in order to exclude the premium from the TILA finance charge. Debt-suspension disclosures must state interest continues to accrue. Pass condition: disclosures given and signed consent obtained before exclusion.
sourceNote: Verified on ecfr.gov and consumerfinance.gov (Reg Z §1026.4(d)); in force as of 2026.

regime: NAIC Credit Personal Property Insurance Model Act (#365)
title: Refund unearned credit personal-property premium on a daily pro-rata basis at cancellation
requirement: An insurer writing credit personal property insurance (e.g., collateral/household-goods coverage on a consumer loan) must, upon cancellation for any reason, refund the unearned premium to the debtor calculated on a daily pro-rata basis, with no refund required below the stated de minimis amount. Pass condition: pro-rata refund issued on each cancellation.
citation: NAIC Model #365, Credit Personal Property Insurance Model Act, § on refunds
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #365 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.

title: Satisfy service-contract provider financial-responsibility requirement (reimbursement policy, funded reserve, or net worth)
requirement: A provider of vehicle/consumer service contracts must demonstrate financial responsibility by one of: (a) insuring all contracts under a service-contract reimbursement insurance policy; (b) maintaining a funded reserve of at least 40% of gross consideration received plus a financial security deposit; or (c) demonstrating net worth/stockholders' equity of at least $100 million. Pass condition: one method continuously satisfied and evidenced to the regulator.
citation: NAIC Model #685, Service Contracts Model Act, § on financial responsibility
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #685 PDF on content.naic.org; ~30 states adopted elements, in force 2026.

title: Register/report as a service-contract provider and file annual accountings with the state
requirement: A service-contract provider must register (or be licensed/report) with the state insurance regulator before selling contracts and file required provider information; where the funded-reserve method is used, the provider must place reserves in an account subject to examination and file supporting accountings. Pass condition: current registration on file and required reports submitted.
citation: NAIC Model #685, Service Contracts Model Act, § on requirements/registration
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #685 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.

regulatorName: Virginia State Corporation Commission, Bureau of Insurance
regime: Virginia GAP Waiver Act (Title 38.2 Ch. 64; NCOIL-based)
title: Refund unearned GAP-waiver charge on cancellation and honor free-look full refund
requirement: A creditor/administrator offering a guaranteed asset protection (GAP) waiver must give a full refund if the borrower cancels within the free-look period with no benefits provided, and refund the unearned portion of the waiver charge upon cancellation or early finance-agreement termination after the free-look period (borrower requesting within 90 days of a terminating event). Pass condition: refunds issued per the waiver and statutory timelines.
citation: Va. Code § 38.2-6404 (Guaranteed Asset Protection Waivers — Cancellation)
sourceNote: Verified on law.lis.virginia.gov (Va. Code 38.2-6404); representative NCOIL-model state, in force 2026.

regime: Florida Limited Surety (Bail Bond) Agent Licensing
title: License limited surety (bail bond) agents and file qualifying power of attorney
requirement: A surety insurer writing bail bonds in Florida must appoint only licensed resident limited surety (bail bond) agents, and the insurer must file a qualifying power of attorney for each agent identifying the surety agent and the company's registered agent. Bail may be written only up to the qualifying power granted. Pass condition: each writing agent licensed and a current qualifying power on file.
citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 648 (Bail Bond Agents); Fla. limited surety agent licensure (2-34)
sourceNote: Verified on myfloridacfo.com licensure PDF; ch. 648 in force 2026.

regime: Connecticut Surety Bail Bond Agent regulation
title: Cap bail-bond agent build-up funds at 40% of premium and hold in trust
requirement: A surety insurer/MGA authorizing surety bail bond agents must limit any build-up fund it requires from an agent to no more than 40% of the surety bail bond premium the agent is authorized to write, deposit build-up funds immediately into a build-up trust account with interest accruing to the agent, and pay the funds to the agent within six months after they become due. Pass condition: build-up funds within the cap, trust-held, and timely returned.
citation: Conn. Public Act on Surety Bail Bond Agents (build-up fund provisions)
sourceNote: Verified on cga.ct.gov bill summary (surety bail bond agents); representative state rule, in force 2026.

regime: NAIC Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act (#360)
title: Deliver individual certificate/policy of credit insurance to each insured debtor
requirement: An insurer writing group credit life or credit A&H must ensure each insured debtor receives an individual policy or certificate of insurance stating the coverage, the amount and term, the premium/identity of the charge, and the debtor's rights, delivered within the statutory period after the debt is incurred. Pass condition: conforming certificate delivered to every insured debtor.
citation: NAIC Model #360, Consumer Credit Insurance Model Act, § on policy/certificate delivery
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC Model #360 PDF on content.naic.org; state-adopted, in force 2026.
